OpenAICompatible.apiKey is mapped with @Convert(converter = EncryptedStringConverter.class). The converter calls Configuration.encrypt / decrypt:

On the first start Configuration writes a random UUID to data folder/secret.key; the AES-256 key is the SHA-256 of that UUID. The file is outside the database, so a database backup alone doesn't reveal the secrets.

A stored value is enc: + Base64 of a random 12-byte IV and the AES/GCM ciphertext. Values without the prefix are read as they are (plain values from before the migration); a value that can't be decrypted (a database from another installation, a different secret.key) is logged and read as null - the user enters the key again.

The converter is a Spring bean: emf sets hibernate.resource.beans.container to a SpringBeanContainer, so Hibernate asks Spring for converters (and entity listeners) and @Autowired fields are injected. Use the same converter for any new secret column.
Code outside JPA (jdbcTemplate, migrations) sees the encrypted value and must use Configuration itself, as EncryptApiKeysMigration does.
Limitation
Consequence
One writer at a time

Writes are serialized; a read-write transaction holds the write lock from its start (see above), so a long one blocks other users' writes (up to busy_timeout, then SQLITE_BUSY); read-only transactions are not blocked. Keep transactions short and never call a model inside one - generation runs outside transactions (@NoTx).
ALTER TABLE is limited
Type, nullability and constraint changes need a table rebuild.
DDL in transactions
SQLite supports transactional DDL, so a failing migration is rolled back completely.
No VACUUM inside a transaction
VACUUM INTO for backups runs with @NoTx.
Dynamic typing
A column accepts any value; the entity mapping is what keeps types consistent.
500 terms in a compound SELECT

The driver answers getColumns of all tables with one compound SELECT, so the columns of all tables together would be limited to 500 (the validation after the migrations hit it with V16). persistence.xml therefore sets hibernate.hbm2ddl.jdbc_metadata_extraction_strategy to individually, validate table by table - keep it.

DatabaseBackupServiceImpl backs up the live database with SQLite's VACUUM INTO 'file', which writes a consistent, compacted copy without stopping the application. Backups go to data folder/db-backups/ as marginalia-time.sqlite (manual) or marginalia-scheduled-time.sqlite; scheduled ones are rotated (keep last N). Configuration writes two more kinds into the same folder, pre-restore-* (the database a restore replaced) and pre-migration-* (see Startup); the service lists every .sqlite file there, and only marginalia-scheduled-* counts as scheduled. The methods the UI calls (create, list, download, upload, delete, restore, schedule) call AdminGuard.requireAdmin(); the scheduled run (createScheduledBackup) and the rotation need no logged-in user.
A database can't be replaced while it's open, so restoring is done in two steps:

DatabaseCheck.check(File) is run on Upload Backup (importBackup), on scheduleRestore and on start. It opens the file read-only and refuses it (InvalidDatabaseException, an IllegalArgumentException with the reason) when:
it doesn't start with the SQLite header,
PRAGMA integrity_check reports problems,
core tables (users, settings, manuscripts, messages, lorebooks, entries, ais, protocols, tags, t2e) are missing - another application's database,

flyway_schema_history has a failed migration or a version newer than the newest bundled migration/V*__*.sql - a database of a newer Marginalia version. A database without the history table predates Flyway and is baselined at V1 as usual.

Configuration.applyPendingRestore() migrates the restored database itself, before the datasource is created, with the same Flyway configuration as the flyway bean (DatabaseCheck.flywayConfiguration(DataSource), used by datasources-config.xml too). If the check fails, the staged file is moved to db-backups/rejected-restore-time-marginalia.sqlite and the current database stays. If the migration fails, the restored file is moved there as well and the pre-restore-* database is moved back. Either way the reason is logged as an error and Marginalia starts with the previous database. A backup from an older version is upgraded on start.
API keys in a backup are encrypted with the installation's secret.key (see Encrypted columns). A backup restored on another installation loses them unless secret.key is copied along.

Tests don't touch your data: MarginaliaTestBase starts the Spring configuration with the data folder in target/test-home/ctx-*, so every test context gets a fresh database migrated by the real Flyway configuration. See Testing.

The service layer holds Marginalia's logic: everything the UI does to data goes through a service, and services are the main API extensions use. This page describes how services and repositories are built, how transactions and the current user work, and what each service is for. The generation engine has its own page, Generation pipeline.
Interfaces live in domain/service/ (and domain/security/service/), implementations in .../impl/. Code always depends on the interface.
Beans are declared in META-INF/spring/services-config.xml. Each entity service gets its repository injected through the repository property; everything else is @Autowired inside the implementation.
Repositories (domain/repository/impl/Jpa*Repository) contain the JPQL and native SQL. They are called only by their service.

Transactions are short. SQLite allows one writer at a time (see SQLite limitations); a long write transaction blocks every other user's writes. Books: search and sort (searchManuscripts → ids; searchRegularManuscripts and searchAgenticManuscripts leave out or keep only the working copies of agents, likewise findAllRegularForUser / findAllAgenticForUser), findViewable(uuid) (own or published, for the viewer), markOpened, the effective prompts of a book (getMasterTemplate, getPov, getTense, getStyle, getUserPrompt, getSummaryPrompt, getMetaSummaryPrompt, getRedraftPrompt, getAnnotatePrompt, getImpersonatePrompt: book value → the folders above it → user default → Defaults; they are resolve(book, PromptField).value(), and resolve / resolveLanguage also say where the value comes from, see Folders), update(book, BookChange) (loads the stored book and applies one change, so a stale copy does not overwrite other settings), moveToFolder, findRegularInFolder, getFavorites / setFavorite, setAgenticCopyFolder, the effective backup strategy, and the JSON form of a book used by backups (createBackup, cloneFromBackup, restoreBackup); delete(book, false) also soft deletes its parts, their summaries and its tags. updateSettings(book, BookSettings) changes the named settings (name, description, language, pov, tense, style, the four prompt templates) and saves: the templates are checked first, an invalid one refuses the whole change (IllegalArgumentException), unknown names are warnings in the result (SettingsSaved); the AI, the protocol, the lorebook and publishing are not among them. createAgenticCopy returns an AgenticCopy (the copy, the UuidPairs, the base backup), cloneFromBackup(backup, pairs) reports the pairs. searchAdvanced(ManuscriptSearchCriteria, sorters) is the advanced search of the book list (name, tags to include/exclude with all/any, dates, number of parts in SQL; the text through ChatMessageService.findManuscriptsWithText, in the active branch or in all branches).
ChatMessageService

createSummary(book, part, callback) streams a summary from the model into a new Summary and attaches it to the part when finished; returns a CancellationToken. The streaming starts after the transaction that inserts the Summary commits (TransactionSynchronization.afterCommit), because the callback thread saves the row as soon as the model answers. createMetaSummary(book, from, to, callback) does the same for a meta summary: it merges the summaries in use between the parts from (newest) and to (oldest, rounded to the end of its block), puts the result on from (attachMetaSummary) and returns null when there is nothing to merge. removeSummary(part, unwind) deletes the summary of a part, restoring the one a meta summary replaced when unwind is set. updateSummaryText edits a text and counts its tokens again. collectBlocks(branch) splits the branch into the summary blocks in use (with their hashes, SummaryBlock.isValid()), collectTree(...) returns the same as a tree of SummaryNodes with the summaries a meta summary stands in for as children (the overview uses it). collectFirstBlock(partsNewestFirst, BlockTexts) gives the first block of a branch with the hash it would have if the story had the texts of the BlockTexts (BlockTexts.CURRENT: as saved), without walking the whole branch. revalidate(book, branch, only) stores the hash of the outdated summaries of a branch again (the command revalidate-summaries), revalidate(book, blocks) that of the given blocks, as ChatMessageService.PartEdit.outdated() returns them after an edit (the checkbox of RedraftDialog); both refuse a book an agent works on. copySummary for branching. softDeleteForManuscript / softDeleteForMessages soft delete summaries in bulk for the delete of a book or parts. See the summary chain.
ExporterService
FolderService
Generating parts, see Generation pipeline.

Images in backups. A stored backup is JSON and never contains image files, only the imageAttachments of the parts (resource uuids) in their extendedContent. ManuscriptBackup.imageCount is a header field (read by parseMetadataOnly without loading the backup) so the UI knows whether to ask. BackupImages reads and rewrites the attachments inside the backup JSON (collect, remap where returning null drops the image). exportBackup(backup, withImages, onImage) writes to a temp file and returns a BackupExport; with images it is a ZIP: backup.json (the stored file, streamed), resources.json ({version:1,resources:[{uuid, entry, name, mimeType, hash, size}]}) and resources/n.ext, one image at a time with Files.copy, so nothing but the JSON tree is in memory. Import, restore and analyzeLorebooks detect a ZIP by its first bytes (openSource) and read entries only by the names the manifest lists under resources/ (no extraction to disk). Each image is read bounded by MAX_IMAGE_BYTES and goes through ResourceService.uploadImage, so it is validated again and the hash dedupe reuses an existing file. Resources are not shared by books, so: importBackup keeps a uuid the user already has with the same hash and otherwise adds the image (adopting), restoreAsNewManuscript and cloneBackup(..., withImages) make a new Resource for every use (from the archive, or ResourceService.copy of the user's own resource, which points to the same file); images that can't be found are dropped from the parts. After every restore linkImages notes the new parts in the resources whose link is empty or stale. The ZIP is only a transfer format, a stored backup stays a JSON file.
ImpersonateService

Imports the .md files of a zip archive (read by utils.MarkdownArchive: natural order of the paths, an optional names.txt for names): appendParts adds a part for each to the end of a book, importLorebook makes a lorebook with a disabled entry for each. Not one transaction (@NoTx): every part or entry is stored by its own createPart / save, so the import can be stopped (BooleanSupplier stopped, asked before each file) or fail and what was stored stays; onStored reports the progress and the ImportResult says how many files were imported. The UI runs it in a ProgressBarDialog with a Stop button (ArchiveImportRunner).

Lets a model annotate a part (the twin of RedraftService). annotate(book, part, Request, Callback) builds the messages from getAnnotateSystemPrompt(book) (the system message), the story before the part (as user and assistant messages, like the generation) and getAnnotatePrompt(book) (the last message), rendered with AnnotateTemplateData: the same story around the part as the redraft, StoryAround, plus annotateInstructions, annotations (the open ones the part has, AnnotationTexts.openAnnotations) and outputFormat) and asks in one of four Modes: STRUCTURED (InferenceService.infer with the class Findings, one retry with the invalid answer and the errors told to the model, then onUnreadable(raw, reason)), DELIMITED (a stream of quote and note blocks separated by ---, read by parseBlocks: quotation marks dropped, a [type] tag, a block without a quote is a note about the whole part, NONE is nothing), TWO_STAGE (a free critique streamed, then the second AI of the request, or the first, turns it into Findings with the part and the critique) and AUTO (structured, delimited when the service can't infer, i.e. throws UnsupportedOperationException). Nothing is stored: the Proposals (quote, note, type and where the quote was found in the part) go to onFinished; accept(book, part, proposals, label) makes the annotations of the chosen ones (source AI). defaultOptions() is the AI and the protocol of UserSetting.defaultAnnotateModel / defaultAnnotateProtocol (null parts: the book's). ContextInsufficient as for the redraft.

Lets a model write the instructions of the next turn in the place of the author (the twin of RedraftService, for a turn that does not exist yet). impersonate(book, Request, Callback) builds the one message of getImpersonatePrompt(book) (rendered with ImpersonateTemplateData) and streams the answer to a Callback (onProgress, onFinished, onTerminated, onError); returns a CancellationToken, null when the book has no AI or protocol, and throws ContextInsufficient when the prompt does not fit. The Request is the guidance (instructions), the outline (a plan of the story a caller gives; the Arc Outline gives its current chapter), the turn details of the next turn (null takes them from the last part of the active branch), another prompt and the GenerationOptions. The story is the active branch (StoryAround: summaries for the older part, the newest parts as far as the room goes), the lore is the one stored on its last part, and the instructions of its last three parts that have some are given as examples of how the author writes. A book with no part yet works. Nothing is stored: ImpersonateDialog and /impersonate take the text.

ManuscriptReplaceService
ManuscriptService

redraft(book, part, instructions, callback) asks the model of the book to write a part again (any part, not only the last one) and streams the answer to a RedraftService.Callback (onProgress, onFinished, onTerminated after a stop with what arrived, onError); returns a CancellationToken, null when the book has no AI or protocol. redraft(..., withAnnotations, callback) also gives the open annotations of the part to the prompt (the variable annotations, one line each: the passage in quotes and the note); RedraftDialog asks for it and resolves them when the text is applied; it can also revalidate the summaries the applied text made outdated (SummaryService.revalidate). Nothing is stored: applying the text is ChatMessageService.updateResponse. The prompt is getRedraftSystemPrompt(book) as the system message, the story before the part as user and assistant messages (StoryAround.messages, as the generation sends it: a server that keeps what it read continues from the start of a message of the user) and getRedraftPrompt(book) as the last message, both rendered with RedraftTemplateData: the part, the instructions, the story before the part (the room for it is rounded down to a step of a sixteenth of the budget, StoryAround.stableRoom, so that the start of the story does not move with the length of the part; the valid summary blocks of the branch up to the part and the parts after the newest of them, newest first until the room is used; with an outdated block no summaries at all), as much of the story after the part on the active branch as fits in a quarter of the room, the lore stored on the part and the data of its turn. RedraftService.ContextInsufficient when the prompt without any story is more than the AI takes (TokenLimits.promptTokens). Checks that the part belongs to the book of the user and has text (IllegalArgumentException) and that no agent works on the book. redraft(..., withAnnotations, passage, callback) redrafts a RedraftService.Passage(start, end) (offsets in the text of the part, IllegalArgumentException when outside it or blank) only: RedraftTemplateData.selection / selectionBefore / selectionAfter are set (the built-in prompt marks the passage in the part and asks for the replacement alone, onFinished gets that text, not the part) and with withAnnotations only the open annotations that Passage.overlaps are given.
RedraftService

Registry of story exporters (registerExporter, unregisterExporter, getExporters). The built-in TxtExporter, MarkdownExporter, HtmlExporter, DocxExporter, PdfExporter and EpubExporter (package export, all extend ExporterBase) are registered in afterPropertiesSet; an extension can register its own Exporter and it shows in the export dialog. See Story export.
Responsible for

Search and replace in the text of a book, in two steps. plan(book, options, progress) (read only) finds the parts of the story and, if asked, their summaries that have a match (the active branch, or all branches), works out the new texts and the new hashes of the summaries and returns a Plan (items(), hitCount(), outdatedSummaries()); apply(book, plan, progress) does it in one transaction and skips what was changed since the plan (Result.skipped()). The database narrows the candidates down by _fulltext (LIKE of the literal text; a regular expression has no such prefilter), the @Fulltextable fields of the loaded entity are then searched by EntityTextSearch (so it works for any entity, a lorebook would only need its own service) with TextSearch (literal, case sensitive or not (Options.caseSensitive(); the _fulltext prefilter is skipped for a text that ignores the case and has non-ASCII characters, as SQLite's LIKE ignores the case of A-Z only), or regex, always as typed, TextHit has the text around the match and the replacement). The hash of every summary of the book is worked out with the changed texts (SummaryService.collectFirstBlock): a summary that was valid and is in the searched scope (summaries searched and its part in the searched branches) gets the new hash, one that was valid and is out of the scope would become outdated and is counted in outdatedSummaries(), one that was outdated stays so. With Options.revalidateSummaries() the hash of every summary of the book (any branch, touched or not, valid or not) is set to what it should be, so nothing becomes outdated. Options.story() off (Options.summariesOnly(...), the search of the summaries overview) leaves the parts of the story alone and looks only into the summaries; the hashes of the meta summaries that stand in for a changed summary are still worked out with the new text. The summaries are searched where the overview shows them: the summary of a part and, inside a meta summary, the summaries it replaced (replacedSummary, serialized, nested for meta summaries of meta summaries; the database can't narrow those down, so every summary of the scope is loaded). A match in them is a hit of the meta summary that holds them, apply searches them again to count their tokens, and no hash is made of them, so nothing is revalidated for them. TaskProgress reports to the caller and asks whether to stop (CancellationException).

SillyTavernImportService

Stores the tree built by utils.SillyTavernChats from SillyTavern chat files (parse reads one .jsonl: header line, then messages with swipes / swipe_id, system messages skipped; merge(chats, mergeTurns) puts the chats into one trie keyed by the instructions and text of a turn, so the shared beginning of branches and checkpoints is stored once and the swipes of a message are siblings; mergeTurns makes the user messages before an answer its instructions). importTree is @NoTx like the archive import: every part goes through ChatMessageService.addPart (counts tokens and words, adds a child or one more first part, does not touch the active leaf), stopped is asked before each part and onStored reports the progress; the active leaf of the book is the end of the chat whose last message is the newest, or the last part stored when stopped earlier. The UI is SillyTavernImportDialog (multi file upload, name, the merge checkbox) and SillyTavernImportRunner (progress with Stop), started by NewBookAction.runFromSillyTavern.
StoryGenerationService
SummaryService

The annotations of a part (see Annotation). create(book, part, start, end, text, source, type, label) (white space at the edges of the passage is left out, IllegalArgumentException for a range that is not in the text; both null: the whole part), createFromQuote(...) (the quote is found with QuoteFinder, not found: the whole part, notLocated), listForPart, listForManuscript, update(book, annotation, text, type, sendToPrompt) (null leaves a value, an empty type clears it), setStatus (not to ORPHANED), reattach(book, annotation, start, end) (an orphaned annotation becomes open), remove (soft delete). Every method checks that the book is the user's and the part or annotation is of that book. The anchoring hooks shift, moveToPrevious, relocate, copyForBranch and the bulk deletes are called by the services that change the text, see the domain model; marshalForManuscript / restoreForPart(part, annotations[, pairs]) are for the backups and the working copy of an agent (pairs collects the uuid pairs of the copy).

The automatic book backups (BackupStrategy.AFTER_N_MESSAGES / AFTER_N_MINUTES) are triggered by the story editor after a part is generated (ManuscriptStoryPart), not by a service - code that generates parts without the editor doesn't take them.

The folders of the books and the settings they pass down: create, rename, move, delete (the content moves up, or deleteWithContent), update(folder, Details), the lists and searches, paths, the copy and move of books and folders (transfer) and the lock against agents. See Folders.

The same two steps for the entries of a lorebook (plan(lorebook, options, progress), apply(lorebook, plan, progress)), with LorebookEntryService.findFulltextsContaining(lorebook, literal) for the _fulltext prefilter. Name, text and comment of the entries (all @Fulltextable fields) are searched; deleted entries are not.

The story tree: createRoot, addChild, insertPart(book, after, text, input) (a part between a part and what follows it: the new part is saved as a child of after, then reparentChildrenExcept / reparentRootsUnder move the continuations under it; no part is deleted or made again, the active leaf moves only when after was the leaf; a parent is therefore not always older than its child, nothing may rely on the order of ids), createPart, getBranchFromLeaf, getSwipesForMessage (siblings), swipeTo (sets the book's active leaf to the deepest last descendant - the caller saves the book), branch (copy as sibling), deleteNodeAndMigrateChildren, word and token sums, countWords. delete(part, false) soft deletes the part with its summary and everything below it, softDeleteForManuscript(book) all parts and summaries of a book with one bulk update (the book's delete uses it). searchFulltext(book, query) finds parts of all branches by their _fulltext (see Full-text search); findLeafFor(book, part) picks the end of the branch that shows a part. findFulltextsContaining(book, literal) and findSummaryFulltextsContaining(book, literal) give the id and _fulltext of the parts (or of their summaries) that contain a text (null: all), for the search and replace. updateResponse(book, part, text) is the edit of a part (tokens, words, edited, save) and returns the part and the summaries that became outdated by it (PartEdit; StorySupport.saveEditedResponse delegates to it); isSummarized(book, part) says whether a summary describes the part (the part itself or a newer part of its branch has a block that reaches down to it), so the redraft dialog knows whether to offer revalidating; previewMergeIntoPrevious(book, part) and mergeIntoPrevious(book, part, input, join, fromPrevious, dropped) join a part to the one before it (the text with a PartMerge.Join, the original text and the images appended, the prompt fields as the author edited them, attributes through PartMerge.mergeAttributes: the later part wins, fromPrevious / dropped are paths of values; then deleteNodeAndMigrateChildren; IllegalStateException for a first part and for a parent with swipes; the pure parts are in domain.components.PartMerge, the review is PartMergeDialog for the desktop and the phone tab); branchAndSwitch(book, part) and swipeAndSwitch(book, part) do what the Branch button and choosing a swipe do and save the book with the new active leaf; they, like the edit, refuse a part of another book. getBranchTokens(leaf) counts the stored tokens of a branch without and with its valid summaries (BranchTokens: the summaries and the parts after the newest valid block; the stale blocks only counted), for BranchTokensDialog. findManuscriptsWithText(ids, query, allBranches) tells which of the books have a part with all the words of a FulltextQuery (the books of the current user only).

ExportDialog (opened from the settings menu of ManuscriptStoryPart) collects the active branch in one ProgressBarDialog (indeterminate), cuts the chosen range and exports it in a second one whose total is the number of messages, then shows the download link. The exporter gets ExportOptions (title, author, title page, language), the messages and the progress dialog, on which it calls updateProgress() for every message.

ExporterBase does the common work: it renders the title page from Defaults.DEFAULT_EXPORT_HEADER_TEMPLATE (Handlebars, data ExportHeaderTemplateData), skips parts without text, reports progress and feeds the Markdown of each part to an ExportWriter that the exporter creates per export - exporters are shared between users, so any state must live in the writer. A part whose text has a Markdown heading is a chapter (chapterTitle, the same rule as the Chapter Marker plugin: the first # line); before the first part the writer gets the list of all chapters in contents(...) and every chapter start in message(markdown, chapter), so it can put an anchor (Chapter.anchor()) on the chapter and link to it from the table of contents (HTML, EPUB navigation, PDF, DOCX; TXT and Markdown ignore it). The PDF exporter keeps the export and renders it again until the pages shown in the contents match the pages the chapters landed on; DOCX uses PAGEREF fields and sets updateFields, so Word fills them in after asking. Images attached to a part (ChatMessage.getImages()) are loaded once per part (ResourceService.findImage + getResourceData, so only the exporting user's images; a missing one is skipped with a warning) and handed to the writer in images(ListExportImage) right after message(...). A part with images but no text is exported with an empty text. HTML embeds them as data URIs, EPUB as files in OEBPS/images/ with manifest items, DOCX with POI pictures (scaled to fit the page), PDF with OpenPDF images, TXT as [Image: caption], Markdown as ![caption](data:...) plus an italic caption line. figure(src, caption) renders the XHTML figure. MarkdownExporter is the only one that does not parse: the Markdown of each part is written as it is (raw HTML included, since the output is source and not a rendered format), as blocks separated by an empty line. It also provides toHtml (CommonMark, raw HTML escaped, XHTML safe) and walk, which turns Markdown into paragraphs, headings, code and rules for formats built from styled text (BlockSink; used by TXT, DOCX and PDF). Libraries: CommonMark (parsing), Apache POI (DOCX), OpenPDF with the Liberation fonts (PDF); EPUB is written with java.util.zip.

Responsible for
LorebookService

findAllRegularForUser / findAllAgenticForUser (the lorebooks without or only the working copies of agents; findAllForUser returns both), fillEntries (loads entries with their effective tags for generation and the editor), getSubbooks, delete(book, false) also soft deletes the entries and tags of the lorebook, export / import in Marginalia's format (exportLorebook, importLorebook, marshalLorebooks, analyzeImport, importLorebooks), SillyTavern import (importFromSillytavern, via SillyTavernEntryConverter) and export (exportToSillytavern: the entries of the lorebook and its subbooks, root first, in one world info file; SillyTavernEntryConverter.exportKeys turns a filter into keys, a regular expression into /pattern/flags with the leading Java flags moved after it and \Q..\E quotes escaped), addSubbook, removeSubbook, setSubbooks and createSubbook change the subbooks of a lorebook with the cycle check (LorebookCycleException, wouldCycle); cloneLorebook(book, name) saves a new lorebook with the entries and tags of the book (they go through marshalEntry and unmarshalContent, so the entries get new uuids) and the same subbooks; marshalLorebooks(root, true) marshals the entries with their uuids and copyLorebooks(lorebooks, pairs) reports which copy is which original. save and delete refuse a lorebook locked by an agent (LorebookLockedException, see Agents).
LorebookActivationService

Which entries a generation uses and why (Reason: constant, filter matched, filter found in the content of another entry (LORE_MATCHED, the scan depth of the lorebook), disabled, negative tag, missing tag, filter not matched, and EXTENSION_ACTIVATED / EXTENSION_SKIPPED for what a listener decided): the rules of the generation step that puts the lore into the prompt, shared with /preview-lore-activation and the Preview activation window (evaluateAll, the same passes without events) so that they agree. An entry with ActivationContext.INCLUDE_PARTS also looks into the newest activationParts parts of the story: partsNeeded (the largest of the enabled entries, 0 = the story is not read) says how many to read, recentParts(leaf, count, excludeLeaf) reads them, evaluate(entry, tags, instructions, parts) / evaluateAll(..., parts) take them (the overloads without parts search the instructions only).
LorebookEntryService

getEntriesForLorebook; delete(entry, false) also deletes the tags of the entry. create(lorebook, fields) and update(entry) save an entry and return the problems of its payload template and regular expression as data (EntrySaved, EntryProblem; a broken entry is saved all the same), validate(entry), deleteEntry(lorebook, entry) checks the entry is one of the lorebook; save and delete refuse an entry of a locked lorebook.
TagService

The user's tags: searchTagsForUser, countTagsForUser (for lazy combo boxes), getOrCreateForUser(value), and for the Tags tab of the settings findUsageForUser (every tag with the number of its relations, TagUsage), findRenameConflict, rename (refuses a value another tag already has) and merge(source, target) (moves the relations of source to target, then deletes source). The tags are looked up by uuid among the current user's, so a foreign tag is ignored.
TagRelationService

Attaching tags to any entity (createRelation, removeRelation, with negative for negative tags) and querying both ways (getTagsForObject, getTagsForObjects for the tags of many objects in one query, getObjectIdsForTag, getObjectsForTag); deleteForTag and deleteForObject delete the relations of a deleted tag or tagged object; moveRelations(from, to) re-points the relations of a tag to another one (a relation the object already has with to is deleted instead) and countRelationsByTag counts the relations of each tag of the user.
AILimitService
AIService

CRUD of inference providers with rules in the service: the user's AIs are their own and the shared ones (AI.shared); save / delete accept only the owner (SecurityException otherwise) and shared = true only from an administrator (AdminGuard); a new AI needs canCreate() (administrators, or a user with the permission PermissionType.CREATE_AI, see PermissionService). delete(ai, false) also soft deletes the usages of the AI. cloneAI(ai, name) copies the settings of an own AI with the API key (an OpenAICompatible, or an ExtensionAI with its attributes), not shared, without limits, and goes through save, so it needs canCreate(). isOwnedByCurrentUser(ai) and isAdministrator() are for the UI; the latter reads the flag from the database, because the session's User bean is filled with id, login and name only, so currentUser.isAdmin() is always false in UI code.

forAI(ai) returns the InferenceService for a provider. Implementations are listed in services-config.xml (inferenceProviders), each annotated @SupportedAI(AIType...) with a constructor taking the AI; the instance is cached on the (transient) AI.inferenceService field. An AI of the type EXTENSION (ExtensionAI) is served by the ExtensionAIFactory that an extension registered (registerExtensionFactory / unregisterExtensionFactory, getExtensionFactory(id), getExtensionFactories()): forAI returns null while the extension is not loaded, forAIOrThrow throws InferenceException (EXTENSION_UNAVAILABLE) instead - the generation steps and summaries use it; protectSecret / revealSecret encrypt a secret for the settings of such an AI, see Inference providers from a plugin. getFunctionRegistry() is the FunctionRegistry; addToolRoleResolver / removeToolRoleResolver let an extension change the role the results of function calls are sent with (default tool, a Gemma 4 API wants tool_responses; resolveToolRole(ai) asks the resolvers in the order they were added, the first non-blank answer wins) - the plugin must remove its resolver on unload.
InferenceService
InferenceServices
InferenceSession

Limits of the users of a shared AI, see Limits. findLimits, setLimit (shared AIs only, validated by AILimit.validate()), removeLimit: the administrator who owns the AI only. getLimit(ai) / getStatus(ai) (LimitStatus: limit, tokens used in the period, next reset) are for the current user; the session's User has no uuid, so the service loads it. check(ai, promptTokens, reservedTokens) (the prompt must fit into the sent and total limits; the generated tokens only count once reached, or with a hard limit together with the reserved response) throws InferenceException NOT_AVAILABLE or LIMIT_REACHED; OpenAICompatibleInferenceService.stream calls it first, so every request is covered.

Not a bean: a thread-local scope like UnmeteredScope, opened by the caller around the call that starts a request (try (InferenceSession _ = InferenceSession.open(InferenceSession.ANNOTATE)) { service.stream(...); }) and naming the kind of work (constants GENERATION for a new part, a regeneration and a swipe, IMPERSONATE, ANNOTATE (the second stage of the two stage mode has the scope extract), REDRAFT, SUMMARY, AGENT (scope: the run id), HELP; a plugin uses its own name, optionally with a scope for parallel runs). An inference service asks InferenceServices.currentSessionId() once in the thread that starts the request, and sends the answer in the header X-Session-ID (InferenceSession.HEADER); a request outside of any scope sends none. The id is Configuration.hmac(session-id, userId + : + kind[/scope]) (32 hex characters, a key derived from secret.key): per user and kind, never per book, so a server that keeps a prompt cache by it (or a proxy that saves and restores a slot by it) holds a bounded number of them. null when the thread has no user. See Prompt cache and session id.

One provider: getModels(), testConnection() (model list plus a one-token completion, used by the "Test Connection" button of AIDialog), countTokens / countTokensApprox, stream(payload, protocol, callback). Failures of the provider are InferenceException (classified by Type: authentication, model/URL not found, context overflow, rate limit, server, timeout, connection...; OpenAICompatibleInferenceService.translateException), also passed to callback.onError; InferenceErrors.describe(loc, throwable) / messageOf give the localized text for the UI. OpenAICompatible has the extended attributes requestTimeoutSeconds and maxRetries, applied to the client (read timeout, retries with backoff for 408/409/429/5xx and connection errors). A user message of the payload (LLMChatMessage) can carry LLMAttachments (images as data or URL, WAV/MP3 audio, files), which OpenAICompatibleInferenceService sends as content parts after the text; an attachment it cannot send (audio in another format, audio or a file given only by URL) throws IllegalArgumentException from stream, attachments of other roles are not sent. Streaming is asynchronous; the callback gets chunks (REASONING / RESPONSE) and must call controller.continueInference() to receive the next one. stream(payload, protocol, functions, callback) also lets the model call functions, see Function calls. infer(payload, protocol, callback) is the non-streaming variant: still asynchronous, but InferenceResultCallback.onResult(text, check) gets the whole answer (reasoning is dropped); limits and usage work as for stream. infer(payload, protocol, schema, callback) also sends the JSON schema as response_format (not strict, an additional parameter response_format wins) and validates the answer (markdown fences removed) with StructuredOutputs.validate: SchemaCheck says checked / valid / errors, an invalid answer is still delivered. infer(payload, protocol, SomeClass.class, callback) builds the schema from the class (StructuredOutputs.schemaOf: fields and Jackson annotations, plus @LLMSchema on the class and @LLMField on fields for description, required, minimum/maximum, length and item limits; unannotated fields are required, no additional properties) and calls TypedInferenceCallback.onResult(object, text), or onError with a StructuredOutputException (holds the answer) when it does not match. stream(payload, protocol, schema, functions, callback) only passes the schema to the provider as response_format; the chunks are delivered untouched and nothing is validated (the caller does it, StructuredOutputs.validate); PartialJson.parse(text) reads the JSON that has arrived so far (fences ignored, unfinished strings kept, a key without a value left out) to display it while it streams. Every variant has an overload taking a FunctionSet before the callback: the model may call functions, run by the same machinery as in stream (rounds, MAX_FUNCTION_ROUNDS, onFunctionCall reported on the callback), and the callback gets one result, that of the last round. Only OpenAICompatibleInferenceService implements infer (default: UnsupportedOperationException). Implemented by OpenAICompatibleInferenceService; an empty API key is replaced by the placeholder none (apiKeyOrPlaceholder, also used for the model list of the provider dialog), because the OpenAI client refuses a request without a key and local servers don't check it.

The model can call Java methods (tool / function calling). The functions are the methods of an interface marked @LLMFunction(name, description); their parameters may carry @LLMParam(name, description, required) (without it the parameter is required and named as in the source, which needs the -parameters compiler option the project already uses). The parameter types are anything Jackson reads: primitives, strings, enums, collections, maps, records and beans (fields described with @JsonPropertyDescription).

Functions are asynchronous. Every @LLMFunction method returns void and takes a FunctionContinuationR as its first parameter (hidden from the model, not in the schema); FunctionRegistry.definitionsOf throws IllegalArgumentException for a method that returns a value or does not have the continuation first (or marks it with @LLMParam). The method is called on a worker thread, in the request scope of the caller, and may hand the work to any other thread; it finishes the call with done.complete(result) or done.fail(message | throwable), whenever and from wherever. The first finish wins. done.isCancelled() tells that the request is over. An exception thrown by the method itself is a failed call.
Type
What it does
FunctionRegistry (inferenceServices.getFunctionRegistry())

definitionsOf(type) compiles the interface once - JSON schema of every method's parameters (victools jsonschema-generator, Jackson module, every parameter schema inlined, recursive types moved to the $defs of the function schema), the Jackson types the arguments are parsed into and a method handle - and caches it in a ClassValue, so it lives as long as the interface class (an unloaded extension releases its entries). bind(type, implementation) is cheap and makes a FunctionSet. An interface without @LLMFunction methods, with a name used twice, a name providers do not accept ([a-zA-Z0-9_-]{1,64}), a static method or an unnamed parameter is an IllegalArgumentException.
FunctionSet

The functions of one request, bound to their implementations; and(other) combines sets of several interfaces. call(name, argumentsJson, executor, cancelled) returns a CompletableFutureString: on the executor it parses the JSON object the model wrote into the parameters (unknown properties ignored, a missing optional one is null / 0 / false, a missing required one is an error), calls the method with a FunctionContinuation and completes the future when the method answers, with the result rendered: null as OK, a string as it is, anything else as JSON. Every failure is the FunctionCallException the future completes exceptionally with.
FunctionContinuationT
What a function answers with: complete(T), fail(String), fail(Throwable), isCancelled().
FunctionCallException
A call that could not be carried out; Kind is UNKNOWN_FUNCTION, INVALID_ARGUMENTS or FAILED (the method threw). Its message is written for the model.

OpenAICompatibleInferenceService offers the functions as tools, collects the calls from the stream (they arrive in pieces), and when the answer ends with calls it runs them as a chain of futures: one after the other, each started on a worker thread (with the request attributes of the caller), the next only after the previous one answered through its continuation, and nothing blocks while a function waits. When the last has answered the next request is sent. Cancelling the token (or a dead callback) fails the pending call and ends the request with onCancel. onFunctionCall is called on the thread the function answered on. appends an assistant message with the calls (LLMChatMessage.ofToolCalls, LLMToolCall) and a LLMRole.TOOL message per result (ofToolResult) to its own copy of the payload and sends the request again. The callback sees one stream of chunks and one completion (the text before a call and the answer after it are both RESPONSE chunks), and InferenceAsyncCallback.onFunctionCall(call, result, failed) reports each call. A failing call is not an error of the request: the model gets Error: message as the result and can correct itself. After MAX_FUNCTION_ROUNDS (10) rounds the request is sent with tool_choice: none, so the stream ends with an answer. A cancelled token or a dead callback stops before the next call. Every request of the loop is counted in the Usage separately. A payload that already holds tool calls and results (LLMChatMessage with toolCalls / toolCallId) is sent as it is. The generation pipeline does not offer functions yet; they are for services and extensions that call stream themselves. A service that cannot call functions rejects a non-empty FunctionSet with UnsupportedOperationException (the default of the interface).

Users: authenticate (PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA256 hashes, constant-time compare and the same amount of work for an unknown user, a missing password or a locked account; the first 10 consecutive failures are free, then the account is locked for 1 s, 2 s, 4 s... up to 15 minutes, tracked in User.failedLogins / lockedUntil; a locked account refuses even the right password; authenticate(username, password, clientAddress) also throttles per client address, in memory only: the first 30 consecutive failures from an address are free, then it is blocked with the same 1 s ... 15 minutes back-off for every user name, blocked attempts are not counted against the user, a successful login does not clear the address (otherwise any account holder could reset the count between batches of guesses), entries are forgotten after an hour without failures, the table keeps at most 10,000 addresses (least recently used dropped first) and a restart clears everything; every failure and the moment of a block are logged; see Login throttling), unlock (an administrator's Unlock account checkbox in UserDialog, shown while the user has failures on record: forgets the failures and the lock), changePassword (also resets the lock, drops all saved logins and invalidates the user's other open sessions through SessionManager.runForUsers - the caller's own session is kept; the current password is checked by UserDialog for self edits), clearPassword (removes the password, resets the lock, removes saved logins and invalidates the user's sessions except the caller's, an administrator's reset), isLoginAvailable, isLastAdmin (the last administrator can't be removed or demoted), deleteUser (soft delete, frees the login by renaming it to login#uuid, drops saved logins, renames the data folder to login-deleted; owned data is purged with the user by cleanup), saved logins (generateNewPersistentInfo; authenticateFromCookie hashes the secret once and compares it with every saved login in constant time, a null user takes the same path; a matched login is rotated).

Garbage collection of the files of resources, administrators only (AdminGuard). The files are in data/user folder/images and resources (Configuration.getImagesFolder / getResourcesFolder) and are never deleted with their Resource, so the files of deleted resources and of replaced content pile up. userFolders() lists the folders of the data folder (also the login-deleted ones), listFiles(folder) the regular files of its two resource folders (StoredFile: folder, kind, name, size, modified; links and subfolders are ignored), findUnused(files) the ones whose name no Resource.path has - one query for the paths of all resources, soft deleted ones included (ResourceRepository.findAllPaths), matched by name only because the names are random UUIDs and a deleted user's folder is renamed while his resources stay in the database. getFile, writeZip (entries named by StoredFile.path()) and delete check every StoredFile again (plain names, images or resources, nothing leaves the data folder: IllegalArgumentException otherwise); delete reads the paths of the resources again and keeps the files in use now, returns a DeleteResult (deleted, skipped, bytes). PermissionService (domain.security.service) answers what an administrator allowed a user to do, see Permission. checkPermissions(user, type) is false when the user has no Permission of the type or it is not granted; getPermission(user, type) returns the object (null when there is none, a deleted one does not count); getPermissions(user) lists them. The permission is found by its holder, not by its owner (the owner is only the administrator who gave it), and the user is loaded again through UserService first - the session's user bean is a scoped proxy with an id, login and name only (an unknown or deleted user has nothing). Administrators are not special here, callers that let them do everything check AdminGuard.isAdmin() too (AIService.canCreate, HelpAssistantService). Changing permissions is for administrators: save, saveWithoutEvent, delete and setGranted(user, type, granted) (changes the existing permission or creates one owned by the current administrator) call AdminGuard.requireAdmin(). The migration that created the first ones (PermissionsMigration) does not go through the service, it runs without a user.
The dialog behind the key button of the user list is ui.dialogs.permissions.PermissionsDialog (see UI); the services it uses are PermissionService and SessionManager.reloadUser.

Failed logins are limited twice. Per user (User.failedLogins, lockedUntil, in the database) and per client address (UserServiceImpl.addressFailures, in memory). Both use the same back-off, 1 s, 2 s, 4 s ... up to 15 minutes, after 10 (user) or 30 (address) consecutive failures; the address limit is higher because several users can share an address. A failure counts against the address whatever the user name was, so a password spray over many accounts is stopped even though no single account fails often.
The address comes from UIUtils.clientAddress(Configuration) (LoginCheckRoute.clientAddress() in the login routes), which asks ClientAddressResolver:
The address of the connection is used by default. X-Forwarded-For is ignored, because any client can send it.

When trustedProxies (configuration.properties, or -DtrustedProxies=...) lists the connecting peer - addresses or CIDR ranges - the header is read from the right and the first address that is not a trusted proxy is the client. Entries left of it were sent by the client and are never used. The private network is not trusted by itself.
Host names are never resolved and a bad trustedProxies entry stops the start.
Without a proxy nothing needs to be configured. Behind one, list the proxy, otherwise all users share its address and 30 failures from anyone block everybody for a while.

Registry and dispatcher of commands (the Commands section describes them in full: writing a suite, the command bar). A command is a public void name(CommandContext) method annotated with @Command (commandName; optional humanName, description and llmDescription for agents, availableForAgent (false keeps the command from agents), dataSeverity (a CommandDataSeverity: DESTRUCTIVE, the default, or NON_DESTRUCTIVE, see Data severity), each an L key with a plain-text variant humanNameText... for extensions, see Texts; async, signature, returns); an object with such methods is a command suite. Overloads: methods with the same commandName are forms of one command (same humanName), told apart by signature = @CommandParameterSignature(@CommandParameter(name, type, description), ...); an empty @CommandParameterSignature is a form without arguments, and a method that declares no signature takes any arguments (@CommandParameterSignature(any = true), the default): the objects are in CommandContext.getPositional() and a list of objects can be passed as one argument of type Object ("any"). returns = @CommandReturn(name, type, description) declares the returned value (String.class...; void.class by default). registerCommands(Object) registers all the commands of the suite (or none: it refuses a class without annotated methods, a method that is not public void with a CommandContext as its only parameter, a name with characters other than letters, digits, _, -, ., two forms with the same signature, forms with different human names, a signature that is also any, a duplicate parameter name and a name another object holds) and returns the CommandDefinitions (one per form); a suite is shared by all users and runs in parallel, so it must be stateless: no fields with the state of a run or a user, the current state is read when the command runs from the services and from the session-scoped SessionPoint (getLanguage(), getWorkspace()); unregisterCommands(Object) removes the whole suite, unregisterCommand(String) one command with its forms (an extension does that in onExtensionUnload, the service does not track bundles). The application's own commands (impl.commands.BackupCommands: /take-backup, an async @Configurable suite that backs up the open book and reports its progress with the status lines) are registered in afterPropertiesSet. Running: execute(name, Map) (arguments by name), executePositional(name, List) and executeLine(/name a b) return a CommandRun (a CompletableFutureObject that also holds the two status lines a command sets with setStatus / setSubStatus: getStatus(), getSubStatus(), addStatusListener); the form is chosen by the number of arguments and the closest types (a value that already has the type, then Object, then text converted to a number, boolean, character or enum; ties go to the form declared first by parameter count; a form that takes any arguments is the last resort). A command line separates arguments by spaces, \ is a space inside an argument, \\ a backslash and \ a quote; an argument can be wrapped in double quotes (two words, spaces inside need no escape, is an empty argument, a quote that is never closed runs to the end) (CommandLine.parse / escape). A command with async = false runs on the caller's thread and must call setReturn before its method returns (otherwise the result is null, later calls are ignored); with async = true it runs on a worker thread with the caller's request attributes and the future completes with the first setReturn, from any thread. Cancelling the future stops the run: CommandContext.isTerminated() becomes true (it is true as soon as the future is done, never while a non-async command runs), the worker thread is interrupted and a command that has not started does not start; an async command checks isTerminated() in its loops and returns at once. A throwing command, or CommandContext.fail, fails the future with a CommandException; no form that fits fails it with IllegalArgumentException. CommandHelp (pure; takes a function that localizes L keys) computes the matching names and the forms that fit what is typed, for the command bar. CommandUtils (package utils) gives a command the current state of the session: the workspace, the open book window (the same interface on the desktop and the phone) and the open book, all delegated to the SessionPoint (for an agent session the AgenticSessionPoint holds the book directly). The commands that read the book are one class each in impl.commands.manuscript.read (see Commands that read the book).

Suites of tools for the model that extensions offer to whoever lets the model call functions (domain.service.tool): a ToolProvider is registered under a bundle identifier, a key and a human name (registerProvider), lists its ToolItems (what the user can check; none means on or off), builds the FunctionSet for the checked items (functions(items, ToolRequest)), may bring a default hint, a description and a suite of commands() that the service registers with CommandService and removes with the provider. getProviders lists them as ToolProviderInfo in registration order (items as they are now); resolve(ToolSelection, ToolRequest) turns what the user chose into a ToolSet (the functions of the providers that have something checked, put together with FunctionSet.and, and their hints: the user's replaces the default one) - a provider that is gone, whose checked items are all gone, or that throws is left out, two providers with a function of the same name fail with both names. ToolSelection is the plain-JSON choice (providers: bundle/key → items, enabled, hint) that the owner keeps. OsgiServiceImpl calls unregisterAll with the symbolic name of an unloaded bundle. The UI is ToolSelectionButton and ToolSelectionDialog, see UI. See Sharing data between extensions.

The services behind the Administration screen check on the server that the caller is an administrator, so they stay safe if something other than that screen (an API, an extension) ever reaches them. They call AdminGuard.requireAdmin() (bean in services-config.xml), which loads the current user from the database - the session copy of admin is not trusted, a user demoted or deleted mid-session loses access at once - and throws SecurityException for nobody, a deleted user or a non-administrator. Guarded: every DatabaseBackupService method except createScheduledBackup and getNextScheduledBackup, CleanupService.getReferenceModel/analyze/purge, every ResourceGarbageService method, OsgiService.installPackage/uninstallPackage, and UserService.deleteUser/clearPassword/unlock. Code that runs without a request (the backup schedule, loading extensions on start, registerContributor) is not guarded, and inside these services it calls private unguarded variants (listBackups, removeBackup). A new administrator-only service method calls adminGuard.requireAdmin() first.

The trash: lists soft-deleted objects (find/count with a TrashFilter of owner and type), shows their extended content as JSON and restores them. Implemented by CleanupServiceImpl (same bean as CleanupService) because it needs the cleanup reference model. Not administrator-only: a user is limited to their own objects, an administrator (AdminGuard.isAdmin()) sees and restores everything, and objects of others raise SecurityException. deletePermanently removes deleted story parts and lorebook entries for good (children of a removed part move to its parent). restore also restores the deleted objects the selection owns (messages of a book...) and is all or nothing: an object that depends on a deleted object outside the selection (STRONG and OWNED_BY references it holds, and the OWNS reference of the object that owns it) blocks the whole restore, see RestoreResult.getBlocked(). See Trash.

ManualService (ManualServiceImpl, a plain bean with init-method=load) holds the user manual in memory: the Markdown pages of manual/user that the build packs as classpath:/manual/ (see Packaging). It is global read-only data, so it has no user and no transaction. load() reads every manual/**/*.md and keeps the pages, a missing or unreadable page is only logged. ManualParser turns a page into a ManualPage: removes the front matter, pictures and Retype admonition markers (!!!warning Title becomes a bold **Warning: Title** line), rewrites links between pages to paths in the manual (books/story-editor.md#images, links into the developer manual become plain text) and splits the page by its second and third level headings into ManualSections with the Retype anchors. ManualIndex is an immutable BM25 index over the sections (heading and page title weigh more than the body, light English stemming, stop words dropped, no support for Japanese or Chinese text). getPage tolerates a leading slash, an #anchor and a missing .md, search(query, limit) returns ManualHits, best first.

HelpAssistantService is the model behind the help chat (ui.components.HelpAssistantWidget). getSettings / saveSettings are for administrators (AdminGuard) and keep Settings(aiUuid, ...prompts, adminData) in AppSettings (what depends on the user is in their HELPER permission: Permission.helperApplyLimits and helperInteractions; an administrator without the permission has both off); saveSettings accepts only an AI the administrator owns (IllegalArgumentException otherwise); requests are made without a protocol. isAvailable() and stream(payload, functions, callback) are for administrators and the users with the permission PermissionType.HELPER (target() checks it at every request). The AI is loaded by uuid whoever owns it (the user could not see it), and only while it is not deleted and its owner is still an administrator, which is checked at each request, so a demoted administrator's AI is never handed to everybody. A request is metered (the normal path, AILimitService.check and UsageService.record for the current user) only for a shared AI when the permission has helperApplyLimits; any other request runs in an UnmeteredScope: a thread-local, opened by the caller around the call that starts the request, that an inference service reads once when the request starts (before it moves to other threads) and then skips the limit check and does not count the usage. OpenAICompatibleInferenceService and the google-genai and anthropic plugins do this; an extension AI must too, see AI providers. The tokens of an unmetered request are not counted anywhere: not for the user, not for the owner.

getInfo() tells any user which AI answers (Info(aiName, model, metered), null when unavailable). ask(history, uiState, callback) is what the chat calls: it puts the instructions in front of the conversation, binds HelpTools and calls stream. HelpTools are ManualTools (search_manual over ManualService.search, read_manual_page over getPage; read only, answers cut to a size a small model can use) and get_ui_state(path, deep), which asks the UiStateSource (the page the question comes from; null when there is none, the function then fails with a message the model can read), see Letting the help assistant see the UI. When the the permission has helperInteractions and there is a UiStateSource, ask binds InteractiveHelpTools instead (adds interact_with_ui(path, interactions), which calls UiStateSource.interact) and appends HelpPrompts.INTERACTIVE to the instructions; see Interactions. HelpTools also has read_last_errors(count) (what the user was shown that went wrong, read through UiStateSource.readProblems, see What went wrong); the rules for it are HelpPrompts.PROBLEMS, added to every prompt after the one the administrator may have edited. Manual tools print the address of what they found (URL: next to Page:): ManualPage.url() / ManualSection.url() turn the path in the manual into the address on the published site (ManualPage.WEB_BASE, https://enerccio.github.io/Marginalia/user/, the GitHub pages of the project: books/story-editor.md#images is .../user/books/story-editor/#images; ManualServiceTest checks that every page has its file under docs/), and the default prompt tells the model to cite pages as Markdown links with those addresses only; the widget opens them in a new tab.

The data of the Admin page. With Settings.adminData (AppSettings.helpAdminData, off by default, a checkbox of the Help assistant tab) and an administrator asking, ask binds a second set of functions beside the others (FunctionSet.and), AdminHelpTools: get_admin_data(topic) (extensions, users, backups, cleanup, application) and read_extension_log(extension, lines), with HelpPrompts.ADMIN_DATA added to the instructions. They read through AdminDataSource, implemented by HelpAdminData: the extensions with their state and verification (OsgiService, optional: it is not in the test context), the counts of the users (no names), the database backups and schedule, what CleanupService.analyze() would purge (nothing is changed), memory and uptime, and the last lines (40 by default, 200 at most, 6000 characters) of the log of an extension, found by its name, symbolic name or JAR (OsgiService.readLog). The functions run on threads of their own, so HelpAdminData runs each read in the request of the administrator that asked (ThreadCopyRequestAttributes taken in ask) and checks AdminGuard.requireAdmin() again. Log lines and verification reports go through UiProblem.clean (cut, keys removed), nothing more: the setting exists because they can still carry text an extension wrote, on its way to the AI of the assistant. The books of the user. With UserSetting.helpAssistantBooks (HelpAssistantService.isBooksAllowed / setBooksAllowed, a check box of the panel, off by default) ask appends HelpPrompts.BOOKS and binds a third set, BookHelpTools (list_folder, search_books, get_book_settings), implemented by BookHelpToolsImpl over BookDataSource / HelpBookData (FolderService, ManuscriptService, ChatMessageService, again in the request of the asking user). They return folder names, titles, descriptions and the short settings with their origin, prompts only as custom or built-in, and for a search where the words were found; never a text of a story. Lists are cut (100 entries, 20 matches). See Folders.

The instructions are one of two prompts, for administrators (AdminGuard.isAdmin()) or for the other users: the text in AppSettings.helpPromptAdmin / helpPromptUser or, when that is null or blank, the default (HelpPrompts.ADMIN / USER); saveSettings stores a blank prompt or one equal to the default as null, so a default follows the new version. `` in a prompt is replaced by the list of pages (path, title, 110 characters of the description), a prompt without it gets no index. The settings are installation wide, so a test that saves them must reset them first. It does not store anything. The conversation of the user is the list SessionPoint.getHelpChat() (a synchronized ListLLMChatMessage, user and assistant messages only), which lives and dies with the HTTP session (logout invalidates it). A model without function calling fails the request; there is no fallback to a prompt with searched sections.

They keep their logic in their own classes annotated @Configurable (plugins are compiled with the AspectJ compiler too), which get the application's services @Autowired - for example the Reviewer's ReviewerService.
