StoryGenerationServiceImpl holds the installed steps (from services-config.xml, one per GenerationStepType) and a cached thread pool (threads named Generation thread NNN). Each call creates a GenerationEngine, which implements GenerationController - the object every step works with:
The book; steps replace it with the saved copy after changes.
The chat messages sent to the model (from PREPARE_PAYLOAD).
The GenerationListener of the caller.
The model of this generation: from the GenerationOptions, else the book's. Steps and listeners read the model here, never from getManuscript(); PREPARE_GENERATION loads both again from the database.
The part being generated (from GENERATE_NEW_MESSAGE).
The request context the threads of the generation run in (a RequestAttributes).
The TurnInput and GenerationRequest.

The engine never blocks a thread while it waits - for event listeners, for a question to the user or for the model. Every step is written as a chain of callbacks: it emits an event and passes the rest of its work as the continuation, which the engine runs on a pool thread once all listeners are done:

GenerationStepBase wraps each step: it enters the user's request scope, checks for cancellation and interruption, and turns any exception into listener.onError(e) plus a jump to CLEANUP. Continuations are wrapped the same way. forEachAsync iterates a list in this style (used for lorebook entries, which emit an event each).

Loads the book's inference provider (AI) and protocol and checks that both are set and that InferenceServices has an implementation for the provider type. (The steps get the service with forAIOrThrow: an AI of an extension that is not loaded ends the generation with the error that says to load it.) Otherwise the user gets Book is missing model. / Book is missing protocol. and the generation ends.
Events: BEFORE_PREPARE_GENERATION, AFTER_PREPARE_GENERATION.
Fills a new PrePromptData with the parts of the prompt that don't depend on the story:
the provider's jailbreak (if Needs Jailbreak is on) and its token count,

the book's effective prompts - master template, POV, tense, style, user prompt - each resolved book → the folders above it → user settings → Defaults by ManuscriptService (resolve(book, PromptField), see Folders). The step that creates the new part writes the book back with ManuscriptService.update (it loads the stored book and sets only the global template variables and the active leaf), so settings changed, or a book moved to a folder, while the generation ran are not overwritten.

After AFTER_STATIC_TEMPLATE_DATA (where listeners may replace any of these), it renders the user prompt template with UserPromptData (the four TurnInput fields) into userPromptProcessed and counts its tokens. The first template rendering creates the generation's TemplateContext (see Template context).
Events: BEFORE_PREPARE_CONSTANT_DATA, AFTER_STATIC_TEMPLATE_DATA, AFTER_PREPARE_CONSTANT_DATA.
Activate each entry - an entry is active when all of these hold:

Before the entries are evaluated the step asks LorebookActivationService.partsNeeded (the largest activationParts of the enabled INCLUDE_PARTS entries, 0 when there is none) and reads that many parts with recentParts(activeLeaf, n, excludeLeaf): the non-blank response of the branch from the root to the active leaf, the newest n, oldest first (the leaf is left out for a swipe or a regeneration - it is the part being replaced). With 0 the story is not read. Each entry then takes the newest of the parts it asks for (evaluate(entry, tags, instructions, parts)); the scan of step 4 does not use the parts.
Check

Collect lorebooks: the book's lorebook and, breadth-first, all its sub-lorebooks. Deleted and disabled lorebooks are skipped together with their sub-lorebooks; each lorebook is used once, so cycles are harmless. Render the active entries' payloads as templates with one shared LorebookTemplateData - so variables set in one entry are visible in the following ones. A payload that fails to render is used as it is.
Rule

Scan (only with a scan depth): Lorebook.scanDepth of the lorebook the book uses (clamped to LorebookActivationService.MAX_SCAN_DEPTH, 5; the value of a sub-lorebook is ignored) is how many passes follow. Pass n takes the entries pass n - 1 activated (pass 0 is step 3), leaves out those with preventRecursion or no payload, and evaluates the entries whose verdict is still FILTER_NOT_MATCHED against the raw payloads of those (joined; templates are not run): evaluateInContent gives LORE_MATCHED, the detail being filter - name of the first entry that has it. The pass ends the scan when nothing was activated. Each such entry gets PROCESS_LOREBOOK_ENTRY again (LOREBOOK_SCAN_DEPTH = n) and a verdict a listener replaced counts. The activated entries are in the order of step 2 whatever pass found them. LorebookActivationService.evaluateAll runs the same rules without events (the preview in the lorebook editor and /preview-lore-activation; they take the parts of the picked book / the part given with recentParts).
Skipped when the book has no lorebook. Otherwise:
tags
the entry has no tags, or one of them is a tag of the book (the entry's tags include the tags of its lorebook)
Decides which part of the story goes into the prompt and renders the system prompt.

Summaries. The branch from the root to the active leaf is read, and the summaries on it are collected (oldest first) into SUMMARIES with SummaryService.collectBlocks: a meta summary replaces the summaries it merged, which are skipped, see the summary chain. Each summary stores a hash of the story it covers; when that was changed since, the summary is removed (a meta summary is unwound to the summary it replaced, which is checked in turn) and the user is asked whether to continue without it (listener.askQuestion). The newest part with a summary is the stop part: it and everything before it is represented by the summaries.
Token budget. With TokenLimits:

If baseTokens + reserved ≥ limit, the generation stops with Contextual limit not sufficient. Otherwise parts are taken from the newest backwards - skipping the part being regenerated, stopping at the stop part - starting from baseTokens + reserved and counting each part as its tokenCount + 100. A part is added only if the running total with it stays within limit − 256; the first part that doesn't fit ends the loop. The chosen texts, oldest first, become MANUSCRIPT_CHRONICLE.

Token breakdown. When the budget is computed, the step creates a PromptTokenBreakdown (domain.components) and puts it into the TOKEN_BREAKDOWN property. It holds the raw counts of each section - context, response and prompt limit, jailbreak, system template (the system prompt without lore and summaries), lore, summaries, story, lore in the user prompt, the user prompt and reserved - and what was cut: the parts that didn't fit (cutMessages, cutTokens), without the parts a summary replaces. The counts are measured separately, so they need not add up exactly to the payload.

Notes of the author. The open annotations with sendToPrompt are read once for the book (flaggedAnnotations). A part that is taken into the story brings its notes (AnnotationTexts.promptNotes: the passage in quotes, or the first words of the part for a note about the whole part, and the note), their tokens count against the room like the part itself, so a part whose notes do not fit is cut; the notes of the parts that made it become MasterTemplateData.annotations for the final render (the estimation render has none).

System prompt. The master template is rendered with MasterTemplateData (backgroundLore, summaries, annotations, narrativePov, narrativeTense, style + the template context) into systemPrompt. The estimate above renders it with a fork of the template context, so macros that change variables don't run twice.
Events: BEFORE_PREPARE_CONTENT, BEFORE_SUMMARIES (SUMMARIES can be changed), AFTER_MANUSCRIPT_CONCATENATION (MANUSCRIPT_CHRONICLE can be changed), AFTER_PREPARE_CONTENT.

p: Builds the chat completion messages:

Earlier parts are sent as the model's own previous answers, each preceded by a short placeholder user turn. The final user message carries the instructions. Only the text of the parts is sent: the images attached to a part are not part of it and the model never sees them.

An LLMChatMessage can carry LLMAttachments (images, audio, files) for models that accept them, and the OpenAI compatible provider sends those of a user message as content parts. This step adds none; a listener of AFTER_PREPARE_PAYLOAD can put them on a user message. A message can also carry function calls (toolCalls, an assistant message) or be the result of one (LLMRole.TOOL with toolCallId); the pipeline builds none of them, they are added by OpenAICompatibleInferenceService when the model calls a function, see Function calls.

The prompt of a part in the View prompt dialog

The existing part, cleared (response and originalResponse both). A full copy of it as it was (ChatMessage.copyOf, attributes deep copied) is kept in the ORIGINAL_MESSAGE property first, and its prompt row in ORIGINAL_PROMPT.

The part gets the TurnInput, the model and protocol names, the payload as JSON (stored as MessagePrompt.builtPrompt, shown by Show Prompt), the activated lore (MessagePrompt.backgroundLore) and the request time. The token breakdown gets the tokens of every message of the final payload (as listeners left it, counted with the provider's tokenizer) and is stored as the part's tokenBreakdown (shown by Token Usage, see UI). Parts generated before it existed have none, getTokenBreakdown() is null for them. Compare Prompt (PromptComparisonDialog) compares the stored payload of a part with that of an earlier part of the branch or a swipe (PromptComparison), to show where a prefix cache ends. The template variables of the generation are stored: local ones in the part's attributes, global ones in the book's. The part becomes the book's active leaf, both are saved and listener.onNodeCreated(part) lets the UI show it. The state stays NOT_SUCCESSFUL - until text arrives, the part is only a placeholder that cleanup removes or restores.
Events: BEFORE_GENERATE_NEW_MESSAGE, AFTER_GENERATE_NEW_MESSAGE (the part is available as getMessage()).

Counts the prompt tokens (when the prompt plus the response limit still exceeds the context, the UI gets GenerationListener.onWarning; the request is sent anyway), then calls InferenceService.stream(payload, protocol, callback) inside an InferenceSession of the kind GENERATION (a new part, a regeneration and a swipe share it, so the provider's cache is that of the story; the service sends it as the header X-Session-ID). For each chunk:
reasoning chunks are appended to responseReasoning (REASONING_CHUNK_RECEIVED, the text in REASONING_CHUNK),
response chunks are appended to response and to originalResponse (the text as generated, which later edits leave alone), with approximate token and word counts (CHUNK_RECEIVED, the text in CHUNK),
the first chunk sets the time to first token, the first response chunk the end of reasoning,
the part and the book are saved and the UI gets onReasoningChunk / onResponseChunk and onMetricsUpdated,
once the response has some non-blank text, the state becomes PARTIAL_SUCCESS (reasoning alone doesn't count).

Listeners of the chunk events can change the chunk text before it is appended. The stream is pulled: the inference service delivers the next chunk only after the step calls continueInference(), so a slow listener slows the stream down instead of piling up chunks.

On completion the exact token counts are computed, the state becomes SUCCESSFUL (AFTER_INFERENCE) and the engine moves to CLEANUP. An error goes to CLEANUP too: a failure of the provider (InferenceException, see Services) is reported with onInferenceError (a default method of GenerationListener that calls onSimpleError; the story editor's listener also writes it to the session's problem log for the help assistant) and a localized text of what to fix, anything else with onError.

OpenAICompatibleInferenceService counts every request in the Usage of the user who started it, so the generation, summaries and extensions that call stream are all counted without doing anything. The request carries stream_options.include_usage (unless the AI's additional parameters set stream_options), and the provider's last chunk then reports the prompt and completion tokens. Without a report (the provider doesn't send it, or the request was stopped) the service counts the payload and the text that arrived with countTokensApprox. It is recorded once, when the stream completes, is stopped (terminateInference, cancellation) or fails after some text arrived; a request that fails before any text is not counted. The stream threads have no request, so the service takes the ThreadCopyRequestAttributes of the thread that called stream and records inside it (currentUser resolves).

Before a request is built, stream asks AILimitService.check(ai, promptTokens, reservedTokens) (with our estimate of the payload and the response size the request reserves): a user with the AI not available or over their token limit gets an InferenceException (NOT_AVAILABLE, LIMIT_REACHED) in the caller's thread and nothing is sent, so the steps, summaries and extensions handle it like any provider failure. The limits are described in the domain model.

New part: the book's active leaf goes back to its parent, the part is deleted (children moved to its parent), onCancelled(null). Regenerate: every value of the part is restored from ORIGINAL_MESSAGE (loadFrom, attributes included), onCancelled(part).

Events: BEFORE_CLEANUP (its listeners do not run when the user stopped the generation, like those of every event) and AFTER_CLEANUP, the last event of every generation: it is emitted when the cleanup is done, also when the cleanup itself failed, and its listeners run also when the generation was stopped or interrupted (Events.isTerminal()). Before the cleanup starts the step sets OUTCOME (GenerationOutcome: COMPLETED; CANCELLED when the user stopped it - that wins over an error the stop caused; otherwise FAILED) and, when an error was reported to the user (onError, onSimpleError, onInferenceError of the GenerationListener; the engine wraps the listener in a FailureTrackingListener, so it does not matter which step reported it), FAILURE (GenerationFailure: the first message and the exception). getMessage() of the event is the part with the text that arrived, null when it was removed. The listener of the caller (onComplete, onCancelled) has been told by then.

All templates of one generation - user prompt, lorebook entries, master template - share one TemplateContext (GenerationProperties.TEMPLATE_CONTEXT), created by GenerationStepBase.getTemplateContext on first use. It holds what the macros read: the TurnInput fields, POV / tense / style, the book's name and description, the model name and token limits, the generation type (normal, regenerate, swipe), the story so far (``...), the last instructions and time, the latest summary, and the variables - local ones loaded from the last part of the branch, global ones from the book. Because it is shared, a variable set in the user prompt is visible in lore entries and the master template. See Templating & macros.
Extensions hook into generation by registering listeners:
Rules:

Call chain.next() exactly once in every listener, also when it fails. chain.terminate() skips the remaining listeners of this event and continues the generation; event.terminateEvents() marks the event so the remaining listeners are skipped when next() is called. A listener that calls neither leaves the generation hanging.
A listener may call next() later, from another thread - for example after an asynchronous request of its own.
An exception thrown by a listener is logged and the chain continues with the next listener.

Listeners are global: they receive the events of every generation of every user. Use event.getManuscript() and the current user to decide whether to act, and keep per-generation data in event.getProperties() under a key prefixed with the extension's package.
Listeners run on generation threads inside the user's request scope, so services work; UI changes need ui.access(...).
Unregister on unload - registrations are not removed automatically.

To only watch an event, most of all a hot one such as CHUNK_RECEIVED, register an observer instead: storyGenerationService.addEventObserver(Events.CHUNK_RECEIVED, observation - ...) (GenerationObserver, returns a Registration too). It is called synchronously on the thread that emits the event - for a chunk the thread of the inference stream - before the listeners of the event, so it costs no hop to another thread and takes no part in the chain (no chain.next()). It gets a read-only GenerationObservation (event, getRunId(), manuscript, AI, protocol, message, request, input and an unmodifiable view of the properties), sees the values as the step produced them (a chunk before the listeners changed it) and is also called for a generation that was stopped. It must return quickly, because the generation waits for it, and must not need a request context. What it throws is logged and ignored.

The bundled Author's Note plugin is a complete example: it reserves tokens in BEFORE_PREPARE_CONTENT (PrePromptData.reservedTokens) and inserts a message into the payload in AFTER_PREPARE_PAYLOAD, see Generation events.
"Read back" means the step reads the property again after the event, so listeners can replace or modify the value. GenerationProperties documents each key.

Stop in the UI calls CancellationToken.cancel(). Every step, continuation and chunk checks the token and jumps to CLEANUP, which keeps what was generated so far (PARTIAL_SUCCESS) - or, when nothing arrived yet, removes the new part or restores the regenerated one, like after an error. Only CLEANUP reports the end to the listener.

Errors - an exception in a step or continuation, a failed request - are reported with GenerationListener.onError and also end in CLEANUP. Validation problems (no provider, context too small) use onSimpleError with a localized message; failures answered by the provider (wrong key, context too long...) use onInferenceError, which does the same unless the listener overrides it.
Questions - listener.askQuestion(text, yes, no) lets a step ask the user and continue in one of two continuations (controller.wrapCallback(...)); used for invalidated summaries.
Small changes (prompt wording, lore filtering, post-processing the answer) - an event listener in an extension is usually enough; see above.

Replacing a step - installedSteps in services-config.xml lists one implementation per GenerationStepType. A replacement must emit the same events and properties, call next() / jumpTo() exactly once per path and set the controller state the later steps expect.

A new step needs a new GenerationStepType value at the right position (the order of the enum is the order of execution) and an entry in installedSteps. Steps without an implementation make the generation report NOT IMPLEMENTED.

generation/LorebookActivationTest, GenerationRequestTest, BuiltPromptHistoryTest (which parts of the story are in the prompt for a new part, a swipe and a regenerate), ReservedTokensTest (reservedTokens), FailedGenerationTest (the cleanup rules above) and MetaSummaryTest run real generations against MockLLMServer, an OpenAI-compatible fake with scripted answers, and inspect the request the model received (InferenceCollector) and the parts that were stored. GenerationTestBase / GenerationRun start a generation and wait for it to finish. See Testing.

Every prompt Marginalia sends is rendered from a template: the master template, the user prompt, lorebook entries and the summary prompt. Templates are Handlebars with SillyTavern-compatible macros on top. This page explains how that is implemented and how to add variables and macros. What users can write is documented in the user guide: Prompt templates and the Macro reference.

The texts of the agents are the exception: the system prompt, the compaction prompt and the instructions of an agent (Defaults.DEFAULT_AGENT_PROMPT and the others around it) are plain text, put into the request as they are, with no Handlebars and no macros.
The code is in domain/templates/ (data objects, context, variables), domain/templates/macros/ (translator, helpers, macro registry) and domain/service/impl/TemplateServiceImpl.java.
TemplateService.processTemplate(template, name, data):
Translate the SillyTavern syntax into plain Handlebars (MacroTranslator.translate).
Compile the result with Handlebars. Compiled templates are cached by template text (Caffeine, 500 entries, 24 h after last access), so a lorebook entry is parsed once, not on every generation.
Render it against a Handlebars Context built from the TemplateData (MacroHelpers.createContext).
Post-process the output: {{trim}} markers are removed together with the newlines around them.
Handlebars runs with EscapingStrategy.NOOP - the output is a prompt, not HTML, so quotes, and stay as they are.

isValidTemplate(template, name) only does steps 1-2, so it catches syntax errors. isValidTemplate(template, name, dataClass) also walks the compiled template (Template.collect of variables and sections, in all branches) and reports names that would end in helperMissing (see Template data) in ValidationResult.unknownNames(). They are warnings, isValid() stays true; the UI shows them as the field's helper text (TemplateHints.showWarnings). Names relative to the current context (this, ., ../x, @index) and parameters ({{#if name}}) are not checked.

Each template gets an instance of a TemplateData subclass. Its bean properties (getters declared in the subclass - TemplateData's own methods are excluded) are the template's variables. A field annotated @LocalizedTemplateDescription(loc = L.DESC_TEMPLATE_...) is listed, with that description, in the hints popover of the prompt fields (TemplateHints), followed by the shared context properties the class doesn't declare.
Names are resolved by MacroHelpers.TemplateDataValueResolver, in this order:
a property of the data object - null renders as an empty string,

a property of the shared TemplateContext (povCharacter, presentCharacters, sceneSetting, instructions, narrativePov, narrativeTense, style, manuscriptName, manuscriptDescription) - that is why these work in every template,
an argument-less macro used as a value, so {{#if user}} works like {{if user}},
otherwise the name is missing and Handlebars' helperMissing hook renders the word Error, so typos are visible in the prompt (MacroHelpers.resolves is the same check, used by validation).

Reflection into anything else is blocked: the resolver returns nothing for other names instead of letting the default resolvers call methods of TemplateData (there is deliberately no getTemplateContext() getter).

TemplateContext is the environment macros read: the turn fields, POV / tense / style, book name and description, model name and token limits, the generation type, the story so far (storyMessages), the last instructions and time, the latest summary, the variables, a clock, a random generator and the seed for {{pick}}.

One context is created per generation (GenerationStepBase.getTemplateContext, stored as GenerationProperties.TEMPLATE_CONTEXT) and set into every data object of that generation, so all templates see the same variables. fork() makes a copy with copied variables for renders whose side effects must not count - the token estimate of the master template uses one.

Summaries and meta summaries build their own context (SummaryServiceImpl.createTemplateContext) from the part being summarized (for a meta summary: the part it is stored on); the variable changes made by a summary prompt are not stored. A redraft uses the same method for the part being redrafted.

{{pick}} is stable: the choice is derived from SHA-256 of the book id (pickSeed), the template key (a hash of the template text), the call site and the options. The same template in the same book picks the same option every time; editing the template or moving the macro can change the pick.

Time macros ({{time}}, {{date}}, {{weekday}}, {{datetimeformat}}...) use the context's clock, which is the server's default time zone - UTC in the Docker image - unless an offset is given ({{time::UTC+2}}). MomentFormat converts moment.js patterns (SillyTavern's) for {{datetimeformat}}.
{{trim}} outputs a marker - the word trim wrapped in the private-use character U+E000, so normal text can't contain it - which postProcess removes together with the surrounding newlines.

Most UI classes are not Vaadin components themselves. They are plain classes with a create() method that builds and returns the component tree, and keep references to the fields they need later:
This shape is deliberate:
@Configurable - the class is created with new, and the AspectJ-woven configurer injects its @Autowired fields (services, Localization, the session User). See AspectJ weaving.

@Extendable - the class is instrumented at startup so extensions can run code before and after any of its methods and read its local variables (see Extensions). Small methods with descriptive local variable names (menu, toolbar, detailLayout) are what make a class easy to extend.
Dialogs (AIDialog, ProtocolDialog, UserDialog, LorebookDialog, ManuscriptDialog...) extend Vaadin's Dialog but follow the same pattern: construct with the entity, call create(), then open().

Code that must not care which layout the user has works with the common interfaces: ManuscriptWindow (package ui.dialogs, implemented by ManuscriptDialog and PhoneManuscriptDialog: the book, its model, open/close, the story tab, the state callbacks, asDialog()), ManuscriptSection (package ui.workspace, implemented by ManuscriptPart and PhoneManuscriptPart: getOpenWindow(), the window of the book that is open or null) and Workspace.getManuscriptSection() / getOpenManuscriptWindow(). The session's SessionPoint holds the workspace, and CommandUtils (package utils) reads it for commands: getWorkspace(), getManuscriptSection(), getManuscriptWindow(), getCurrentManuscript() and getCurrentAI() return null when there is no session, workspace or open book. The book-related methods delegate to SessionPoint (getManuscriptWindow(), getCurrentManuscript(), getCurrentAI()), which AgenticSessionPoint overrides for a session without a browser: the book is held directly and there is no window.

Command bar (see The command bar). CommandBar (package ui.components, a Composite) is the input line for the commands of CommandService, to be placed anywhere: a ComboBox with custom values, where the user types /name arg arg, plus a run button. The list is filled lazily from the registry (CommandHelp.matchingNames), the help is a Popover above the bar (it covers what is above and moves nothing in the layout), rebuilt as the text changes (description, the forms that fit, the next parameter highlighted, the return value, "too many arguments"); it opens for the arguments, for text that is not a command and for a name nothing matches, and while the name is typed the list (with the descriptions) is the help; picking a command writes /name into the field, or runs it when it takes no arguments. The bar shows no results: it hands them to its CommandResultTarget (setResultTarget), an interface (onCommandResult, and clearCommandResult when the user types or runs something else) that each place implements as it needs; the story tab (ManuscriptStoryPart.createCommandBox(), next to the menu bar) uses CommandResultView, a popover above the bar with a close button, and other places can consume the value differently. An async command opens CommandProgressDialog (modal, the two status lines of the command, Stop cancels the future); failures and stops are shown by the bar. Not on the phone story tab yet.

Main.proceedWithLogin picks PhoneWorkspace instead when the body of the page is narrower than 768 px (ExtendedClientDetails.getBodyClientWidth()). The choice is made once per login: resizing or rotating the device does not switch the workspace until the page is reloaded, and a tablet or a phone in landscape gets the desktop one. PhoneWorkspace replaces the left-hand tab sheet with an AppLayout: the parts are listed in a drawer (opened with the toggle in the top bar) whose footer holds the language selector, Change Password and Logout, and the active part fills the screen. There is no Admin button and no AdminPart on a phone: the administration (users, database backups, cleanup, extension install) is only reachable in the desktop layout. The services still check AdminGuard.requireAdmin() themselves. The user manual describes this for users in Using Marginalia on a phone. Only the book list, the lorebooks, the settings, the protocols, the models and the trash differ. PhoneManuscriptPart renders the book list like the Viewer (stacked filters, sort buttons, one column) with the controls of ManuscriptPart; both share the Add Book flow in NewBookAction. PhoneLorebookPart hosts PhoneLorebookView, a reduced LorebookView: lorebooks can only be selected (no add, delete, import or export, no new entries) and only the enabled flags and the content of an entry are editable, every other setting of the lorebook and of an expanded entry is shown as text. PhoneTrashPart hosts PhoneTrashGrid (see Trash). PhoneProtocolPart and PhoneAIPart replace the type, name and action columns of their desktop lists with a text column (Type: and Name: on two lines) and a buttons column. PhoneSettingsPart extends UserPart (so the extension settings panels that decorate UserPart.refresh/save keep working) and only overrides createHeader(): the title, the unsaved changes hint and the Discard/Save buttons are stacked, and Import backup as new book is left out. The workspace is autosaved so the next login opens it where it was left. Everything that has state worth coming back to implements Restorable (ui): JsonObject storeState() serializes the state the class needs into a new object and asks the children it has for theirs (nested under their own key), restoreState(JsonObject self) reads it back and passes the nested objects on. RestorableState has the defensive readers (string, bool, strings, object) and put, which leaves out an empty state. Workspace, WorkspaceComponent (default: no state), ManuscriptDialogPart and PhoneManuscriptDialogPart (default: no state), both book dialogs, LorebookView/PhoneLorebookView and NewTurnForm are Restorable. What is stored:

WorkspaceAutosave (ui.workspace, one per workspace) keeps the state in UserSetting.workspaceState, an @ExtendedAttribute(inject = true) JsonObject (so no migration). Workspace.autosave() stores the state of the whole workspace; the parts call it after the user did something worth coming back to - selected a tab, changed a filter, opened or closed a book, selected a tab of the book window (ManuscriptDialog.stateChanged()), opened an entry or chose a lorebook (setOnStateChange of the views), typed into the new turn form (NewTurnForm.setOnChange). It writes nothing when the state did not change, and failures are only logged. Main.proceedWithLogin calls Workspace.restoreAutosaved() after create() and refresh(): the autosave is off until then, because building the workspace fires the same change events and would overwrite the stored state, and it stays off while restoring (the restoring fires them too). The book window is restored after open(): ManuscriptPart.openManuscript is the one place that creates and opens it, for the Edit button and for restoring. Code that saves a UserSetting must load it right before, not hold on to one (UserPart.save does), or it writes back an older workspaceState.

Lazy loading of the parts, a window that slides over the branch. LazyBranch is the plain logic without UI: the size of the window is UserSetting.storyPartsLimit (empty loads everything), a chunk is half of it; tail starts the story with the last parts, head the reader with the first ones, loadEarlier / loadLater extend the window by a chunk and trimLater / trimEarlier drop the parts at the other end, centerOn(id) moves it around a part that is not loaded, moveToTail back to the end, refresh swaps in the instance a card holds now (an edit saves a new one). StoryLazyLoader fills the panel of a story tab with the cards of the window and answers edge-top / edge-bottom of the panel: it adds the chunk, drops the other end (an edited card is saved first; nothing is dropped while a part is generated, because the streaming card is the last one and the branch does not have it) and puts the visible part back in place. scrollTo(id) is the outline (moves the window when the part is not loaded), showTail() is called before a generation starts, so the new part is added after the last one. ReaderLazyLoader does the same for the reader (Viewer) with plain parts that carry data-message-id. Both put a LazyLoadIndicator in the header and footer of the ScrollPanel (setHeader / setFooter) while there is more to load at that edge, so a user who outruns the loading sees it.

A click with Shift ticks or clears the range between the part and the one clicked last (clicked, using that order, so it covers parts that have no card). The box is a MassDeleteBox (ui.widgets), a plain input type=checkbox whose one click event carries both the new checked state and shiftKey (the Vaadin Checkbox sends the click and the value change as separate events, so the Shift state reached the server one click late); it also writes checked back to its element so a later setChecked is not skipped as unchanged. listenTo(panel) only stops the browser from selecting the text between two clicks (JavascriptLibrary.noTextSelectionOnShiftClick). Delete asks (ConfirmDialog), then a ProgressBarDialog without Stop soft deletes on its worker thread: it loads the branch and calls ChatMessageService.deleteNodeAndMigrateChildren for the selected parts from the last part back, passing along the book it returns, so a part is always deleted while the entities before it are what the database has (from the first part on, the children of a deleted part would be moved to the deleted parent of a later one). After it the mode is off and the tab loads the book again. load of another book and a generation (setFrozen(true)) turn it off.

Minimizing (1.6.0). A tab of a detachable dock has a minimize button (makeMinimizable, in the Tab itself). minimize(id) adds the id to the ordered set minimized; the tab keeps its place in Group.ids (so restore(id) puts it back where it was, and a group whose tabs are all minimized is just not shown, like a group whose tabs are not there yet) but presentEntries leaves it out, so arrange() takes its Tab out of the TabSheet and the content only lives in its Entry. isMinimized(Entry) is minimizable minimized.contains(id); setMinimizable(id, false) (the story) is a set of ids of its own, fixed, which also works for tabs that are not in the dock yet. select(id) of a minimized tab restores it. The dock is body (the columns from fill) and bar in a flex container whose direction is the DockSide (LEFT is row-reverse, the bar being after the body in the page; the classes tab-dock-at-*); refreshBar (run by every arrange) rebuilds the bar when the minimized tabs or the side change: the move button (setDockSide(side.next()), one click goes clockwise; a ContextMenu or MenuBar there would need a Vaadin session in the tests) and one icon button per minimized tab (the image is TabDockIcons.dataUri(letters, id), an SVG circle as a data URI whose color comes from the id; the tooltip and the aria label are Restore: caption). getLayout() adds minimized:[id,...] (only when there are some) and dock:top (only when not left) to the layout, setLayout reads them, so onLayoutChange saves them with the book. add(id, caption, letters, content) gives the letters of the icon, the initials of the caption (TabDockIcons.letters) are the default.

It builds a ManuscriptSearchCriteria from the fields (a to date becomes the start of the next day, the end is exclusive) and lists the result of ManuscriptService.searchAdvanced: ManuscriptRepository.searchManuscripts(criteria, …) does name, tags (one EXISTS per tag; include all/any, exclude any/all), dates and the number of parts in one JPQL query, then ChatMessageService.findManuscriptsWithText keeps the books that have a part with all the words (_fulltext LIKEs, as in searchFulltext), restricted to the active branch (ChatMessageRepository.findActiveBranchIds) unless all branches is on.
The automatic backup after N parts / minutes, the limit of parts to load (partsLimit) and the saving of an edited part. The story does not remember a scroll position: it always opens at the bottom.

The card interface both ChatMessageCard classes implement, and the registry of the cards of the branch and the streaming one (opened reasonings, last flags, freezing, autosave; getOffset is how many parts of the branch have no card because they are before the first one, prependAll puts earlier cards in front; the loader sets the offset after it drops cards at the start).

The default layout of the user. Save layout as my default (StoryMenuKeys.SAVE_LAYOUT_AS_DEFAULT, StoryEditor.saveLayoutAsDefault) stores TabDock.getLayout() in UserSetting.defaultStoryLayout (an extended attribute, no migration). applyTabsConfig takes it for a book that has no $desktopManuscriptStoryPartTabsConfig of its own (and does not write it into the book), and so does Restore default layout. PhoneManuscriptStoryPart uses new TabDock(false), one plain sheet.
The dialog holds the book (getManuscript(), refreshManuscript() reloads it, save() saves it) and freeze() / unfreeze(), which disable the tabs, the exit button and every part during generation.

The fields of the New Turn Instructions popover, the turn details of a part, the metadata lines of a part. NewTurnForm.setOnImpersonate shows the Draft Instructions button (the story parts set it to open the ImpersonateDialog), setInstructions, setPovCharacter and setPresentCharacters put a text into the field as if typed (the Character Tracker plugin gives the two character fields a picker button).
The GenerationListener of a story tab: creates and fills the cards while a generation streams, redraws the story at its end. The tab reacts through Callbacks.

The helpers are @Extendable instances (the tabs create them with new, StoryBackup and StorySupport are @Configurable), so a decorator of one of their methods applies to the desktop and the phone tab alike. The inner card classes stay inner classes of the tabs: extensions reach the outer part through this$0.

The search field of the outline of both story tabs: parses a FulltextQuery, finds every occurrence (SearchHighlighter.count in the response of the branch, which it reads through a BranchSource, because the browser's search cannot see parts that are not loaded), numbers them through the branch and keeps the current one (previous / next, Enter / Shift+Enter, status text and progress bar). The cards draw their response through mark(messageId, text) (SearchHighlighter wraps the matches in mark class=search-match, the current one also search-match-current, and leaves the mark tags of Highlight Generated Text alone), so StoryCard.renderResponse is the one place the text is set; StoryLazyLoader.showMatch moves the window to the part, redraws the card and JavascriptLibrary.scrollToSearchMatch scrolls to the mark. refresh(branch) is called when the story is drawn again.

The tab with the id ManuscriptStoryPart.LOREBOOK_TAB (lorebook) of the left bar is the LorebookPreview (ui.components), a read only preview of the lore of the book, desktop only (the phone has the PhoneLorebookView). It is a TreeGrid of Rows (a lorebook or one of its entries) over a TreeData it rebuilds in refresh(lorebook): with the Include sub lorebooks checkbox the lorebook and every lorebook below it (found breadth first like ProcessLorebookStep does, each once, so a cycle ends) are the top level rows and their entries the children, otherwise the entries of the lorebook are the top level rows. The item details of an entry row show the content, rendered with a Markdown component, and the filtering (text or pattern). It saves nothing; the opened entries and the lorebooks the user closed are kept (as uuids) over a refresh. ManuscriptStoryPart.load() refreshes it, and onTabEnter() calls load(), so the lore is read again every time the user returns to the Story tab. Like the other views of this kind the components are built in create(), the injected services are not there in the constructor.

The whole desktop editor is one TabDock (leftBar, the name is older than the story tab): the outline, the lorebook preview, the tabs of extensions and the story itself (ManuscriptStoryPart.STORY_TAB, story; its content is centerLayout: the scroll panel with the cards and the bottom bar with the menus, the command line and the round button) are its tabs, so the user arranges the whole screen. TabDock is a reusable widget: a row of columns, each a stack of tab sheets, whose tabs the user can drag out into sheets of their own (a strip between the sheets of a column) or into a column of their own (a strip between the columns and at the sides) and back (the drag and drop is Flow's DragSource/DropTarget, no JavaScript; the strips show while a tab is dragged). The columns and the sheets of a column are separated by SplitLayouts the user can resize; a split layout has two sides, so the cells of a row or column are a chain of nested split layouts, the position of each being the share of its cell in what is left (chain, shares). When a splitter is dragged the shares of all cells are read again and stored as size (percent of the dock / of the column) in the layout, onLayoutChange saves them; a cell without a size gets the average. Tabs have a stable id (add(id, caption, content), the outline is ManuscriptStoryPart.CHAPTERS_TAB); the layout, {columns:[{size:50,groups:[{size:50,tabs:[id, ...]}, ...]}, ...]} (size optional) (getLayout/setLayout; a layout with groups at the top level, as the dock stored before it had columns, is one column), names tabs only by id and keeps the place of tabs that are not there now, because extensions add their tabs late (a tab the layout does not know goes to the first sheet). ManuscriptStoryPart stores the layout in the attributes of the manuscript under $desktopManuscriptStoryPartTabsConfig (TABS_CONFIG_ATTRIBUTE): saveTabsConfig() runs after a drag or a resize, applyTabsConfig() in load() before the story is drawn. The selected tab of each sheet is not part of the layout but the Restorable state of the dock.

The window of the Draft Instructions button of the new turn form (desktop and phone) and of extensions that know the plan of the story: ImpersonateDialog.open(book, turn, outline, onUse). The guidance (starts as the typed instructions), the read only outline, ImpersonateService.impersonate streamed into a text field the author may change; onUse gets the text. Nothing is stored.

Two things about TabDock that the story relies on. A TabSheet disables the content of the tabs it does not show (Element.isEnabled() is false for it, so the story ignores events from the page while another tab of its sheet is selected; what the server changes in it still reaches the page) and keeps it in the page, hidden, so the scroll position survives a switch of tabs. Moving the tab to another sheet attaches the content anew, and the scripts that watch the edges for the lazy loading are lost, as is the scroll position: StoryLazyLoader.reattached() (called by an attach listener of centerLayout) arms them again and has the story scroll to its end before the response goes out (beforeClientResponse), unless a render or a scroll to a part of the same request decided where the story is (they clear bottomOnReattach), so entering the story tab from the tree still lands on the part that was asked for. And setTabsEnabled(enabled, exceptId) disables the tabs and the contents of all tabs but one (while a generation runs the story stays enabled: its stop button; setFrozen calls it) and only touches the contents the sheet does not manage itself. TabDock.select(id) selects a tab in whichever sheet it is; ManuscriptStoryPart.showStory() does it for the story, and the code that is about to show a part calls it: an entry of the outline, a hit of the search, startGeneration, the next onTabEnter when scrollToMessageOnNextRender asked for a part, and ManuscriptDialog.selectStoryPart (what the tree calls when the user chooses a branch).
What a story tab needs from its dialog (refreshManuscript, save, freeze, unfreeze); ManuscriptDialog and PhoneManuscriptDialog implement it (through ManuscriptWindow).

What the desktop and the phone story editor have in common lives in ui.dialogs.story, so the two classes keep only their layout and the methods extensions decorate (renderStoryContent, createSidebarButton, populateMenuBar, createCogsMenuItem, the card's createMenuItems, refreshSummaryMenuItems, autosaveAndSwapToMarkdown):
The bottom bar of the story editor has a MenuBar with two items, built by small methods so that extensions can add to it (see Extending the UI):

The settings item (field cogsMenuItem, local cogs); its sub menu is built from the registry (MenuKind.TOOLS), the actions are the public methods of StoryEditor (openSearchReplaceDialog, openArchiveImportDialog (an ArchiveUploadDialog, then ArchiveImportRunner.appendParts), openBranchTokensDialog, openExportDialog, toggleBookStyles, setShowGeneratedDiff, setAnnotationsInMargin, confirmRestoreDefaultLayout). The phone tab has the same items without the desktop only ones (highlight, margin, restore layout)

Empty, runs last: the hook for new items of the bar.

The checkable Highlight Generated Text item is the diff view: setShowGeneratedDiff(show) stores the flag (a field of the tab, not saved) and calls ChatMessageCard.renderResponse() of every card, which sets the content of the response Markdown - with the flag on, the text from GeneratedTextHighlighter.highlight(response, originalResponse, CssStyles.GENERATED_TEXT), which diffs both texts word by word and wraps the shared words in mark. The card calls renderResponse() whenever its response changes (construction, streaming, end of an edit), and StoryGenerationListener.onResponseChunk copies originalResponse into the card's own ChatMessage while streaming. The phone tab has no diff view.

SummariesDialog shows the summaries of the active branch (SummaryService.collectTree) in a TreeGridSummaryNode: the summaries generation uses are the top level, the summaries a meta summary stands in for are its children (including the summary it replaced, read from replacedSummary, which has no id). Columns: database id (the hierarchy column), message id, order in the branch, content, tokens, a checkbox and a delete button. Checkboxes, delete buttons and the edit pencil exist only on the top level - the text of the merged summaries is part of the hash of their meta summary, so editing them one by one would invalidate it (the search and replace works them out again).

Content (SummaryContent): reasoning (a Details with Markdown, reasoning is mostly markdown), badges (Meta summary, Replaced) and the text as plain text (white-space: pre-wrap, summaries are not markdown and the model's single line breaks must show), in a scrolling Div of a fixed height, so all rows have the same height. The pencil is in a gutter next to the scroll area (not over the text); it swaps the text for a TextArea of the same size and the buttons for a green check (SummaryService.updateSummaryText) and a red trash icon (back to the Markdown).

Delete goes through SummaryRemoval.confirmAndRemove, shared with the part menu of the story editor: a normal summary is confirmed with yes/no, a meta summary asks Unwind / Delete / Cancel (ConfirmDialog with custom button labels).
Create meta summary takes the ticked summaries, uses the newest as from and the oldest as to and opens SummaryDialog with a meta request (createMetaSummary); it needs at least two.

Search and Replace (menu bar, openSearchReplaceDialog()): the search and replace of the summaries only, see SearchReplaceDialog below for the dialog; it also changes the summaries a meta summary stands in for and the summary a meta summary replaced, and keeps the hash of the meta summaries valid (ManuscriptReplaceService).
The grid is reloaded after every change (refresh()): editing, deleting, replacing, and closing the dialog of a meta summary.

SummaryDialog is the dialog of one summary: it generates it (startGeneration, streaming into a read-only text area, with a Stop button), or shows the existing one. It is created with the part, and with the oldest part of the range for a meta summary. It was an inner class of ManuscriptStoryPart; both the story editor and the overview open it now. Both dialogs are @Configurable(preConstruction = true) (they use injected services in their constructors) and @Extendable; the overview's menu bar above the grid is empty, populateMenuBar(bar) is where extensions add tools.

Lists of entities use Vaadin Grid with a lazy data provider. BackendTableProviderBase (in ui.widgets) is the common base: the owning part searches for the ids to show (ManuscriptService.searchManuscripts(...) returns ids, already filtered and sorted), passes them with setIds(ids), and the provider loads only the entities of the visible page (service.find(id)) and wraps them in a BackendTableItem subclass. It also tracks checked rows.

A Chart.js chart: setChartConfig(json) takes a Chart.js configuration (type, data, options) as JSON and draws it responsively into the element (height 320px, the chart-js style). Used by TokenUsageDialog (doughnut of the prompt sections, bar chart of the payload messages), opened from Token Usage in the part menu of the desktop and phone story editors.

A ContextMenu whose items are made when it opens: the constructor takes the target and a beforeOpen runnable that onBeforeOpenMenu runs before Flow sends the menu. The menu of a story card is one (see createHamburgerMenu / prepareMenu of the cards), so a story of hundreds of parts does not create the items of all of them.
A Cytoscape.js graph with rings around a center node and re-centering by double click, see Custom components.

A model and a protocol combo box (the AIs and protocols of the user, the protocol optional) for a dialog that runs the model with a choice of its own: setSelection(ai, protocol) / getAi() / getProtocol() / addSelectionListener(Runnable) / setPlaceholder(text). Used by the generator dialogs of the Lore Generator and the Arc Outline. On a phone the two boxes are full width, the protocol under the model.

Puts a language on many books, the item Mass Change Language of the same menu of ManuscriptPart. The same list as MassChangeModelProtocolDialog (check boxes with check all, name with the name filter, language), a ComboBoxLanguage instead of the picker, and a replace() that sets Manuscript.language (an extended attribute, so it is saved through ManuscriptService.save) on the checked, shown, unlocked books.

Puts a model and/or a protocol on many books, opened from the Mass changes menu (MenuBar, item Mass Change Model/Protocol) of ManuscriptPart. A ModelProtocolPicker whose empty boxes show Do not replace (setPlaceholder) and a grid of rows (check box with a check all box in its header, name with a name filter in the header row, model, protocol) from ManuscriptService.findAllRegularForUser, sorted by name. The filter keeps shown, and a book it hides is unchecked, so Replace and exit changes only what is visible; the check all box ticks the shown, unlocked rows. replace() loads each book again by uuid, sets only the model and the protocol that are picked, saves it through ManuscriptService.save and calls the onChange callback (the book list refreshes). Locked rows (AgentRunService.findLockingRun) are grayed out (CssStyles.MULTI_TAG_LOCKED), can not be ticked and are skipped, the lock is asked again at the change.

Puts one tag on many books, lorebooks or the entries of a lorebook (Kind.BOOKS, Kind.LOREBOOKS, or the constructor with a Lorebook), opened from ManuscriptPart and LorebookView. A ComboBoxTag (an unknown typed value is made with TagService.getOrCreateForUser) and a grid of rows (check box, name, chips of the tags with the picked one marked, apply / remove buttons); the rows with the picked tag sort first. The tags of all rows come from one TagRelationService.getTagsForObjects; apply and remove go through createRelation / removeRelation with the class of the entity (Manuscript, Lorebook, LorebookEntry), positive relations only. A row is locked when AgentRunService.findLockingRun returns a run (an entry is locked with its lorebook); locked rows are grayed out (CssStyles.MULTI_TAG_LOCKED), can not be ticked and are skipped when the change is made, which asks the lock again as the run may have started since the list was read. The tag relations themselves are not guarded by the services, so the lock is checked here.

The Branch Tokens item of the settings menu of ManuscriptStoryPart / PhoneManuscriptStoryPart: a stacked bar (ChartJs) and a table of ChatMessageService.getBranchTokens against TokenLimits.promptTokens of the book's model and protocol. Not @Extendable.

The button next to the LanguageSelector in the workspace footers: toggles UserSetting.themeMode (ThemeMode DARK / LIGHT, dark when not chosen) and applies it with Page.setColorScheme; ThemeSwitch.apply is also called by Main.proceedWithLogin, so the scheme is set when the workspace opens. Only the current page changes at once.

The clone button of the book list (ManuscriptPart, PhoneManuscriptPart): the name of the copy (the book's name and (Copy)) and Only current branch; Clone calls BackupService.cloneManuscript(source, name, onlyCurrentBranch) and gives the new book to setOnClone, which the book list uses to read itself again. The lorebook is linked, not copied.

The common way to let the user choose the tools the model may use (ToolService). The button keeps a ToolSelection (setValue / getValue / addValueChangeListener, the listener gets the new choice when the user saves), shows Tools (n) with the number of things that are on, hides itself while no suite is installed (refresh() looks again; it also does on attach) and opens the dialog. The dialog has a Details section for each ToolProviderInfo under its human name with the number checked: a lazy multi-select grid with a filter field of its own (the checked items stay whatever the filter says; Check shown / Uncheck shown instead of a select-all, which would check the hidden rows) for a suite with items, one check box for a suite without, and a collapsed text area for the hint of the suite (its placeholder is the default hint). It edits a copy and gives the new ToolSelection to its callback on Save. Used by the Lore Generator and the Arc Outline generators.

The folders of the book list: the rows of the grid, the settings of a folder and of a book (PromptSettingsForm is the Prompts tab of the book, desktop and phone, and the body of FolderDialog), the two-pane Organise window, the question of a name clash and the names of books in combo boxes. All described in Folders. The grid of ManuscriptPart holds FolderBookRows (a folder or a book), so a plugin that read its items as Manuscript must read FolderBookRow.getBook().

The help chat: a round robot Button fixed in the bottom right corner (CssStyles.HELP_FAB) opening a fixed panel above it (HELP_PANEL: header with clear and close, which AI answers, a warning when Info.metered(), the check box Let the assistant look at my books with its notice (booksBox, read by loadBooksAllowed when the panel opens and saved by saveBooksAllowed through HelpAssistantService.setBooksAllowed), the messages, an input row whose send button turns into stop). Added to Main after the workspace, so the phone layout has it too; hidden unless HelpAssistantService.isAvailable() when the page is built, the panel reads getInfo() at each opening. Answers stream into a Markdown card with ui.access + UIPushGuard.push; the conversation is SessionPoint.getHelpChat() (the widget keeps the list, the callbacks have no session). A request that fails or is refused (limit) takes the question back into the input field and shows the reason in the card. Reasoning chunks are not shown.
The language combo box of the workspace footers: saves the choice in UserSetting.language, sets SessionPoint.language and reloads every page of the user (Localization).

The Mass edit of LorebookView: one GridRow with the entries of a lorebook and of its subbooks (LorebookService.getLorebookTree, the lorebook first, each once), sorted by LorebookEntry.order, then by the position of the lorebook in the tree, then by name. A Row is an entry with the lorebook it is in and whether that lorebook is locked (AgentRunService.findLockingRun(Lorebook), asked for each lorebook of the tree, as a subbook can be used by another book than the root). The cells change the enabled flag, name, order (the grid is sorted again), tags, filtering mode, filtering, insertion mode, negative tags and note (the fields of the detail row of LorebookView) in place through LorebookEntryService.save; the lorebook cell and the Move checked button call LorebookEntryService.move, which refuses (LorebookLockedException, shown by UIUtils.internalServerError as a warning) both a locked source and, since this dialog, a locked target lorebook. The text is StringUtils.abbreviated to CONTENT_PREVIEW_LENGTH and kept on one line by CssStyles.MASS_EDIT_CONTENT. Locked rows use CssStyles.MULTI_TAG_LOCKED and are never targets. The onChange runnable (the view's refreshEntries) runs when the dialog is closed after a change.

The pieces of the import of .md archives (story part, new book, lorebook; the service is ArchiveImportService). ArchiveUploadDialog.show(title, message, handler) takes a zip file in memory and calls the Handler; an IllegalArgumentException of the handler (not a usable archive) is a warning and the dialog stays. ArchiveEntryNamesDialog.show(content, onConfirm) lists the files with the entry name each would get (names.txt, the first heading, the file name) in an editable grid and hands the names over in the order of the files. ArchiveImportRunner runs the import behind a progress dialog with Stop (what was imported stays, the user is told how much).

The Preview activation of LorebookView and PhoneLorebookView: a text area (lazy value change), an optional book to take the tags from (TagRelationService.getTagsForObject) and a grid of LorebookEntryVerdicts from LorebookActivationService.evaluateAll(root, collectLorebooks(root), tags, text, parts) (parts: recentParts of the active leaf of the picked book, as many as partsNeeded says, none without a book) - the used mark, name, lorebook, order, scan pass and the localized reason (Localization.getActivationReason, keys ENUM_ACTIVATION_REASON_*) with its detail. The summary counts the used entries and their tokens (TokenizerService.countTokensApprox of the raw payload). Read only, nothing is saved, no events: what extensions change in a generation is not shown.

The read only Lorebook tab of the desktop story editor: a tree grid of the lorebook (optionally with its sub lorebooks as top level rows) and its entries, opening to the content and the text activation. create(), then refresh(lorebook).

The Redraft item of the part menu of ManuscriptStoryPart / PhoneManuscriptStoryPart (the method redraft of the card): the instructions of the author, the redraft streamed by RedraftService.redraft into a text field that can still be edited (a ResizableTextArea, value change mode LAZY), a WordDiffView of the changes (worked out again from the text whenever the author edits it, not while the model streams), and Apply, which stores the text with ChatMessageService.updateResponse and hands the saved part to the card (it draws the response and the metrics again). When ChatMessageService.isSummarized says a summary describes the part, the window has the checkbox Revalidate the summaries this redraft makes outdated (off at first): Apply then passes the summaries of PartEdit.outdated() to SummaryService.revalidate, so the edit does not leave them outdated. RedraftDialog.open(book, part, passage, onApplied) redrafts a selected RedraftService.Passage only: the selected text is shown, the diff is against it, and Apply (replacePassage, which keeps the whitespace at the edges of the passage) puts the text in the passage after checking that the stored text is still the one the passage was selected in. It is offered by the right click menu of the text of a card (CardAnnotations, which finds the selection and gives the passage to the card's redraftSelection; the menu ☰ is not used because it takes the selection away). Closing the dialog stops a running redraft. Not @Extendable. Opened by openAuto (the automatic annotation) the dialog puts the redraft (reasoning, text field, WordDiffView) into a TabSheet tab and the part as it was in a second tab, TextMarkup.apply over StoryAnnotations.marks (the marks of the story, read-only), with the open notes listed under it; only the selected tab's content is attached, so find the second one with TabSheet.getComponent.
The Tags tab of UserPart: a grid of the tags with their relation counts, rename (a name that exists asks to merge) and delete. It acts at once and is not tracked as an unsaved setting.

The version text (Marginalia 1.5.0 (93ec118)) as a Span fixed in the bottom left corner (CssStyles.BUILD_INFO_FOOTER, 10 px, faded, outside the layout); the tooltip has the full commit id, the commit time and the build time. Added to Main after the workspace (the phone layout has it too). The login overlay shows the same text as LoginI18n.additionalInformation (LoginCheckRoute.getLoginI18n). The values come from utils.BuildInfo, see Building.
The workspace's left-hand tab sheet with a footer area.

Widget

TrashGrid is a self-contained widget (@Configurable, create it with new TrashGrid(allUsers).create()) over TrashService: a lazy multi-select GridTrashItem (items identified by their EntityKey, so the selection survives paging), a filter by type (names from Localization.localizeDomainObject(Class)) and, with allUsers, a filter by owner and an owner column. allUsers only decides what the widget shows; the service decides what the current user may see and restore. Restore Selected confirms and calls TrashService.restore; when it returns blockers the widget shows them in a dialog (nothing was restored), otherwise it refreshes and runs the listeners from addRestoreListener (TrashPart uses it to refresh the whole workspace). Delete Permanently (createDeleteButton, the field deleteButton) is enabled while the selection has only types of TrashService.getPermanentlyDeletableTypes() (story parts, lorebook entries), confirms and calls TrashService.deletePermanently, shows the reasons in a dialog when it is blocked and refreshes the table otherwise (nothing to refresh elsewhere, nothing came back). The Extended Content link opens the JSON from TrashService.getExtendedContent in a read-only text area. TrashPart (the Trash tab, allUsers for administrators) and CleanupPanel (a Details section, created when first opened) both use it.

PhoneTrashGrid (used by PhoneTrashPart) subclasses it through the createToolbar() (it adds the same createDeleteButton()) and addColumns() hooks: the filters are stacked over the whole width, the description is behind an info button (a Popover) instead of above the table (createDescription()), and the table has only the check box column and one content column that shows name, type, owner (allUsers), delete time and the Extended Content link below each other.

Generic dialogs: ConfirmDialog.show(message, onYes), TextInputDialog.Builder, ListSelectDialog, ErrorDialog (message and expandable stack trace), ProgressBarDialog, SearchReplaceDialog. DialogFocus.onOpen(dialog, field) (ui.widgets) puts the cursor into the field a dialog is about every time it opens, so the user can type at once; the form dialogs (AIDialog, ProtocolDialog, UserDialog, ExportDialog, TextInputDialog, ListSelectDialog, AILimitEditDialog, SearchReplaceDialog) call it. ExtensionLogDialog.show(bundle, name) is the read-only, monospace view of an extension's log. UsageDialog.show() is the read-only table of every user's Usage (administrators). AILimitsDialog.show(ai) is the table of the limits of a shared AI with add / edit (AILimitEditDialog) / delete, AILimitInfoDialog.show(ai) the current user's limit and usage of it.

SearchReplaceDialog (ui.dialogs.search) is the search and replace window without any knowledge of what it searches. A subclass supplies the title, its own options (createOptions(), shown next to the regex option and locked with it) and createSearcher(SearchRequest), which runs on the UI thread (the place to read the options) and returns a Searcher for the worker thread; that gives a SearchResult (the rows as SearchReplaceItems with their TextHits, an optional warning to confirm before the replace, and the Replacer that does the work). The dialog goes through the states INPUT → SEARCHING (inputs frozen, only Stop works) → PREPARED (inputs locked, Search is Search again, which drops the result, and Replace works; a warning goes through confirm) → REPLACING (everything frozen) → INPUT; the work runs on a ThreadAccessDialog thread and reports to the progress bar through TaskProgress. The constructor flag phone selects the layout (the fields and buttons below each other, one column in the table), so one class serves both layouts. ManuscriptSearchReplaceDialog adds the summaries and all branches options and calls ManuscriptReplaceService; the story parts of both layouts open it from the settings menu and show the story again when onReplaced fires. The third constructor argument summariesOnly is for the summaries overview (SummariesDialog and PhoneSummariesDialog open it from their menu bar item Search and Replace, openSearchReplaceDialog(), and load the overview again on onReplaced): it has no Search in summaries box and calls the service with Options.summariesOnly, so the story is not searched. LorebookSearchReplaceDialog is the second subclass, for the entries of a lorebook (no extra options, getIdColumnHeader() makes the table show entry names); LorebookView has a button for it after Add Entry and PhoneLorebookView an icon button.
